title: POST /control/{action} and /plan/apply take raw dicts: a non-numeric hours or soc_pct is a 500, unknown fields pass, and an unvalidated day_local is stored
label: bug
steps: As an operator: POST /api/sites/<id>/control/hold with body {"hours": "four"} (or {"soc_pct": "abc"}, or {"hours": {}}). `float(inp.get("hours", 4) or 4)` on line 154 and `float(inp.get("soc_pct") ...)` on line 161 raise ValueError/TypeError, which no route-level handler catches; api.py's catch-all (line 317-321) turns it into 500 'The server could not answer this request'. Same shape on POST /plan/apply (line 94: raw dict, `str(inp.get("day"))[:10]` accepts any junk as the day_local key that control_state later matches against today).
expected: HANDOFF §4 'Strict models: request models forbid unknown fields. A refusal is a Refusal(status, sentence, code)'; plan Part 2.8 untrusted input; the page expects a one-sentence 422 it can show in the dialog (control-actions.tsx line 100).
actual: A malformed body is a 500 server fault with a request id, logged as a crash; unknown fields are silently accepted; `day` is stored unvalidated (e.g. 'yesterday' or '2026-13-45').
evidence: routes_plans.py:152-168 (`inp: dict = Body(default={})`, float() calls); routes_plans.py:94-103; api.py:317-321 generic except -> 500. Contrast sites.OverrideFields (sites.py:366-370) which is a Strict model, and routes_sites.overrides_post which uses it.

verdict.reason: REPRODUCED live as operator with the api.py client: POST /api/sites/6d4db49bf87e/control/hold body {"hours":"four"} -> 500 {"code":"server_error","request_id":...}; POST .../control/pause body {"hours":[1]} -> 500. float() on routes_plans.py:154 runs before auth.need and before sites.add_override, so nothing was written (overrides list checked empty afterwards). Contrast on the same site: POST /overrides with an unknown field -> 422 'Unknown field' (sites.OverrideFields is a strict model). The catch-all is api.py:315-321 (logs 'unanswered_request', answers 500). Unknown fields are silently accepted (`inp: dict = Body(...)`, routes_plans.py:94 and :152; a bogus action with an extra field reached the 404 branch without any 422). On /plan/apply, routes_plans.py:98 passes `str(inp.get('day') ...)[:10]` and plans.mark_applied (plans.py:641-654) validates method and photo but never day_local, so a junk day is inserted into `applied` and will never match control_state's `day_local = today()` (routes_sites.py:47-49) nor be confirmed. Note `{"hours": {}}` from the finding's steps does NOT crash (`{} or 4` -> 4); the other two cases do. No DESIGN_LOG entry or HANDOFF 8/9 item covers it; HANDOFF 4 'Strict models: request models forbid unknown fields' is the stated convention and plan Part 2.8 / SIT-01 ('422 in a sentence on every bad field') the requirement. Severity medium rather than high: the page's dialog validates and sends numbers (control-actions.tsx:53-60) and the apply dialog offers only compiled days, so a user cannot hit it from the UI; it is an API-contract/robustness defect plus unvalidated stored data for API callers.
verdict.corrected_title: POST /control/{action} and /plan/apply take raw dicts: a non-numeric hours or soc_pct is a 500, unknown fields pass, and an unvalidated day_local is stored

"""Round 7, the control page's API (audit pages-B-01, pages-B-06): the control actions and "mark as applied" read their bodies through strict models (a
bad field is a 422 in one sentence, never a 500, and nothing is written), an applied day is a date of the plan's table, and the write budget counts the
Karachi day, not the UTC date."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone

import pytest

from gridlytics import sites, store
from test_fix_api import world  # noqa: F401  (world is a fixture)

PKT = timezone(timedelta(hours=5))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("action,role,body,said", [
    ("hold", "operator", {"hours": "four"}, "The hours must be a number"),
    ("hold", "operator", {"soc_pct": "abc"}, "The soc pct must be a number"),
    ("release", "operator", {"hours": [1]}, "The hours must be a number"),
    ("hold", "operator", {"hours": 2, "colour": "red"}, "Unknown field 'colour'"),
    ("hold", "operator", {"hours": 500}, "The hours must be at most 72"),
    ("hold", "operator", {"soc_pct": 140}, "The soc pct must be at most 100"),
    ("pause", "admin", {"hours": [1]}, "The hours must be a number"),
    ("resume", "admin", {"hours": "x"}, "The hours must be a number"),
])
def test_a_control_action_with_a_bad_field_is_a_sentence_and_writes_nothing(world, action, role, body, said):
    r = world.c[role].post(f"/api/sites/{world.site}/control/{action}", json=body)
    assert r.status_code == 422, (r.status_code, r.text)                  # 500 "server_error" before
    assert r.json()["detail"].startswith(said) and r.json()["code"] == "invalid"
    with world.use():
        assert sites.overrides(world.site) == []


def test_a_control_action_checks_the_action_then_the_permission_then_the_body(world):
    sid, op = world.site, world.c["operator"]
    assert op.post(f"/api/sites/{sid}/control/explode", json={"hours": "x"}).status_code == 404
    assert op.post(f"/api/sites/{sid}/control/pause", json={"hours": [1]}).status_code == 403      # an operator does not pause
    r = op.post(f"/api/sites/{sid}/control/hold", json={"hours": 2, "soc_pct": 60})
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.json()["control"]["key"] == "hold", r.text
    with world.use():
        (o,) = sites.overrides(sid)
    assert o["kind"] == "reserve" and o["value"] == 60.0 and o["reason"] == "Operator hold"


def _plan_with_days(w, days: list[str]) -> str:
    t0 = int(datetime.now(timezone.utc).timestamp()) // 900 * 900
    iso = lambda t: datetime.fromtimestamp(t, timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    with w.use(), store.connect() as con:
        con.execute("INSERT INTO plans (id, site_id, generated_at, belief_time, valid_from, valid_until, mode, status, summary, steps, slots) "
                    "VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)", ("p-r7", w.site, iso(t0), iso(t0), iso(t0), iso(t0 + 86400), "a", "active", "{}", "[]",
                                                       json.dumps({"brand": "deye", "days": [{"date": d, "slots": []} for d in days], "fallback": None})))
    return "p-r7"


def test_marking_a_plan_applied_takes_only_a_date_of_its_table(world):
    sid, op = world.site, world.c["operator"]
    today = datetime.now(PKT).date()
    days = [today.isoformat(), (today + timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()]
    pid = _plan_with_days(world, days)
    for body, said in (({"plan_id": pid, "day": "yesterday"}, "The day is a date written YYYY-MM-DD"),          # stored as "yesterday" before
                       ({"plan_id": pid, "day": "2026-13-45"}, "The day is a date written YYYY-MM-DD"),
                       ({"plan_id": pid, "day": "2020-01-01"}, "This plan has no table for 2020-01-01"),
                       ({"plan_id": pid, "day": days[0], "by": "someone else"}, "Unknown field 'by'"),
                       ({"day": days[0]}, "The plan id is missing"),
                       ({"plan_id": pid, "day": 20261109}, "The day must be text")):
        r = op.post(f"/api/sites/{sid}/plan/apply", json=body)
        assert r.status_code == 422 and r.json()["detail"].startswith(said), (body, r.status_code, r.text)
    with world.use(), store.connect() as con:
        assert con.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM applied").fetchone()[0] == 0
    r = op.post(f"/api/sites/{sid}/plan/apply", json={"plan_id": pid, "day": days[1], "method": "vendor_app"})
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.json()["day_local"] == days[1], r.text
    r = op.post(f"/api/sites/{sid}/plan/apply", json={"plan_id": pid})                              # the day defaults to Karachi's today
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.json()["day_local"] == days[0], r.text

title: Advisory tier: the table to key in is re-compiled every 15 minutes with no stable daily table, no record on the page of which table was keyed, and a write budget that is never counted or enforced for keyed tables
label: feature-gap
area: Control: vendor table / Mark as applied
steps: At an advisory_writes site (e.g. the demo textile plant), open /sites/:id/control, copy the table, mark it applied for today. Wait for the next tick (15 min; or press Re-solve now). Reload Control: `comp = plans.current(site_id)['slots']` now shows the new plan's table (different boundaries after a forecast update), the header still reads 'Following plan (table applied)' (control_state keys on any applied row for today), and nothing on the page says which table the installer actually keyed or that today's keyed table differs from the one shown.
expected: Plan Part 7.1 step 7: 'the nightly table write after the 23:00 solve; an event rewrite only when the expected rupee gain exceeds a threshold (default Rs 500), the budget allows and the previous write is more than 60 minutes old'; Part 7.6: the installer keys the day's table and the product confirms that table from telemetry; UI-15 'the capabilities card with budgets used today'. The installer needs one stable daily table (plus an explicit 'a better table is worth Rs X, re-key?' nudge).
actual: delivery.compile_mode_a is run on every tick and the control page always shows the current plan's table; `budget.used_today` counts plan_messages rows, which are written only on an edge key pull (routes_edge.py:410-427), so at a keyed-table site it is always '0 of 3' and never enforced; the applied log links a plan_id but the page never shows that plan's table against the current one. The tracker marks DLV-01 (write budget, 60-minute spacing) as [~].
evidence: routes_plans.py:133-148 (control: `comp = (p or {}).get('slots')`, `writes_today` from plan_messages); routes_sites.py:47-52 (control_state 'following' on any applied row today); vendor-table.tsx:52-68 (days from control.compiled, table of the current plan); plans.py:391-470 (every tick compiles and stores slots; no budget logic); EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md:185 DLV-01 [~].

verdict.reason: REPRODUCED by code and the live payload. plans.tick (plans.py:391-470) compiles delivery.compile_mode_a and stores the slots on every tick; scheduler.py:71 ticks at :00/:15/:30/:45; GET /control (routes_plans.py:136-137,144-145) always serves plans.current's slots and vendor_view, and vendor-table.tsx:52-68 draws that; so at an advisory site the 'table to key in' changes under the installer every quarter. Live: Faisalabad (deye, advisory_writes) control = {'key':'following','label':'Following plan (table applied)'} with applied [] (demo_link short-circuit, routes_sites.py:47-50; at a real advisory site any applied row for today gives the same label whatever plan it names). budget.used_today = 0 of 3 at both advisory demo sites: routes_plans.py:141-142 counts plan_messages, which are written only by plans._record_send (plans.py:670-673) from the key-only edge pull (routes_edge.py:408-419), never by a keyed table; grep for budget/threshold/60-minute/Rs 500 logic in plans.py, delivery.py, scheduler.py finds none. The applied log (mark-applied.tsx:95-118) shows day/by/method/confirmation, never the applied plan's table against the current one. Mitigating fact: the confirmation replays the applied row's own plan_id (verify.confirm_applied, verify.py:846), so the savings gate is coherent with what was keyed; the defect is on the control page and in the absence of a daily table/nudge. BY-DESIGN check: the write budget and 60-minute spacing are explicitly part of tracker DLV-01 '[~]' (EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md:185) and HANDOFF 8.C points to the tracker for [~] items, so that half is a listed open item; but the user-facing moving-target behaviour at the installer-keyed tier (plan 7.6: 'the installer keys the day's table'; 7.1 step 7; UI-15 'budgets used today') is in neither DESIGN_LOG nor HANDOFF 8/9 and is new evidence of impact at v1's only real delivery path. Medium: a real flow (keyed-table delivery) is wrong/misleading, not money or safety.

fix_proposal.fix_summary: At the advisory tier, issue one stable table a day (from the first solve at or after 23:00 the night before) and re-issue today's only when the twin-replayed gain is at least Rs 500, the brand's table writes allow it and the last issue is an hour old. Record each issue in a new table_issues table. Serve the issued table on GET /control, with its issue and the blocked re-issue, and count issues as the day's writes. Flip the chip to 'New table issued' when a re-issue follows the mark. Mark-as-applied records the issued plan.
fix_proposal.approach:
Root cause: plans.tick recompiles and stores a Mode A table on every tick. GET /control (routes_plans.py:136-148) always draws plans.current()'s table, so the 'table to key in' changes every 15 minutes. budget.used_today counts plan_messages, which only the edge's key pull writes, so at a keyed-table site it is always 0. control_state reads 'Following plan (table applied)' for any mark today, whatever table it named. Plan 7.1 step 7 (nightly write after the 23:00 solve; an event rewrite only above a threshold, inside the budget and 60 minutes apart) and 7.6 (the installer keys the day's table) are not modelled.

Fix (backend):
- store.py schema v3 adds `table_issues(id, site_id, day_local, plan_id, issued_at, reason, gain_rs)`. store._connect copies the file before migrating, which satisfies the 'back up before schema changes' rule.
- plans._issue_tables runs in tick after an active plan is stored, at advisory sites with a battery:
  - At or after 23:00 local, if tomorrow has no issue, it issues tomorrow's table as 'nightly'.
  - If today has no issue (new site, after a pause, failed nightly solve), it issues today's as 'first'.
  - Otherwise it computes _reissue_gain: the energy cost of the issued table minus the new one. Both are replayed through the twin on this tick's forecast over the whole horizon, with this plan's later days behind each, so the energy either table leaves in the battery is priced the next day. This mirrors the compare drawer's pricing.
  - It re-issues ('event') only if gain >= REISSUE_THRESHOLD_RS (500, overridable per site by data.reissue_threshold_rs), today's issues < BRANDS[brand].table_writes_per_day, and the last issue is >= 3600 s old.
  - The decision ({gain_rs, issued, blocked}) is saved on the plan summary as `reissue`.
- plans.issued_view swaps each compiled day for the issued plan's day.
- GET /control returns `issued` and `reissue` (gain_rs is stripped for viewers by the existing `_rs` filter) and counts issues as used_today at the advisory tier. The closed-loop tier keeps plan_messages.
- control_state answers 'unconfirmed' / 'New table issued: key it in and mark it' when an 'event' issue is newer than today's mark.

Fix (frontend):
- The vendor table says when and why the day's table was issued, or that the day is still a draft.
- A Notice explains when a better table is waiting (spacing or budget).
- Mark as applied sends the issued plan_id for the chosen day. Before, it sent control.plan_id, the current draft.

This keeps the DESIGN_LOG rule that plan_messages rows are written only by the edge's key pull, and it does not touch the signed message or Mode B. Closed loop is unchanged. The remaining part of DLV-01 [~] (ranking boundaries by twin value, HANDOFF 8.A.2) stays open.

Alternatives considered:
- (a) A stopgap that only pins the table of the applied row and diffs it against the current one: it still gives no daily table before the mark and no budget.
- (b) Keeping the issues in site state JSON: no migration, but no history or audit and it needs pruning.
- (c) Re-issuing on any change: this is today's behaviour.

The 23:00 hour, the threshold and the 60-minute spacing are the plan's stated defaults.

Shared context with pages-B-08: after this fix a mark names the issued table's plan, which is what B-08's early check replays.

Validated: the backend edits compile; test_fix_r7_issued_table.py passes when run by hand against a patched scratch copy; two real ticks at an advisory site (23:05, then 10:00) issue 'nightly' and then record a below-threshold re-issue decision; and tsc --noEmit passes on the patched web app. The full diffs are /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f64857cc-0ca7-5cbb-b665-d2b474fb2fb8/scratchpad/audit/r7fix/per/B-02.backend.diff and B-02.frontend.diff.

title: grid_cap_w (the MDI cap) is dropped from every vendor layout, yet the twin enforces it: a keyed Deye/Growatt/Sungrow table cannot peak-shave, and `mdi_not_enforceable` is never reported
label: spec-mismatch
area: Control: vendor table / Mode A compiler
steps: Site with a Deye inverter and an MDI tariff (demo Karachi feed mill). GET /sites/:id/control: each compiled slot carries `grid_cap_w` (delivery.py:193-196) and the twin honours it (twin.py:213-214, 296), so the wrong-plan guard, the compare drawer and the advisory confirmation all simulate a device that caps grid import. vendor_view (delivery.py:219-227) emits program/time/power_w/soc_pct/grid_charge/gen_charge for Deye and slot/start/end/mode/soc_pct for the rest: no grid cap, and `max_discharge_w` is the plan's max discharge (line 170), not `max(0, Lhi - mdi_cap_kw)`.
expected: Plan Part 7.1 step 4: on Deye, Growatt and Sungrow (no peak-shaving primitive) set each peak-risk slot's max_discharge_w to at least max(0, Lhi - mdi_cap_kw) and the floor so that energy is available; where the brand cannot hold both, 'the expected MDI rise is reported on the plan as mdi_not_enforceable, so the savings page never credits a peak cut the device could not make'.
actual: The keyed table has no cap at all; the plan's summary never carries mdi_not_enforceable; the compare drawer and savings MDI lever assume a cap the installer cannot key. DESIGN_LOG (v1 build) says 'every slot carries grid_cap_w (the plan's MDI cap) so the device peak-shaves to it', which only holds for an edge that reads grid_cap_w, not for Part 7.6's installer-keyed delivery, which is the only delivery in v1.
evidence: delivery.py:170-171, 182-196, 212-228; twin.py:200-214, 296; DESIGN_LOG 'Mode A compiler (Part 7.1)' bullet; BRANDS[deye].mdi_primitive False (delivery.py:29-30).

verdict.reason: REPRODUCED by code and live data. delivery.py:193-194 puts grid_cap_w on every slot (live: Faisalabad deye slot grid_cap_w 326273; Lahore huawei 461324; Karachi sungrow 901965); twin.slots_policy honours it (twin.py:213-214) and twin.simulate peak-shaves to it (twin.py:296, 348-349); vendor_view (delivery.py:219-227) emits program/time/power_w/soc_pct/grid_charge/gen_charge for deye and slot/start/end/mode/soc_pct otherwise: no cap in any keyed row (live vendor rows confirm). max_discharge_w is the plan's max discharge (delivery.py:170,185), not max(0, Lhi - mdi_cap_kw). grep -rn mdi_not_enforceable over backend/gridlytics finds nothing. plan_compare (routes_plans.py:120) and the demo twin at advisory sites (demo.py:161-167, slots_policy of the current plan) therefore simulate a capped device the installer cannot key; the capabilities card itself prints 'Demand (MDI) limit in the inverter: No' for deye while the table silently carries one. Site reference in the finding is off: Karachi feed mill is sungrow/closed_loop; the Deye+MDI case is Faisalabad (advisory_writes). BY-DESIGN: DESIGN_LOG 'Mode A compiler (Part 7.1)' bullet (docs/DESIGN_LOG.md:272) documents 'every slot carries grid_cap_w so the device peak-shaves to it' and the 'charge slot's demand cap' bullet (line 88-90) refines it; this is a deliberate decision, but it only works for an edge that reads grid_cap_w, while plan 7.6 says v1 delivery is installer-keyed and 7.1 step 4 requires the Deye/Growatt/Sungrow translation plus mdi_not_enforceable so 'the savings page never credits a peak cut the device could not make'. Kept with design_wrong=true. Medium not high: real-site savings price measured telemetry (verify.py MDI lever from actual peaks), so money is not over-credited there; the compare drawer and the demo's advisory-tier figures are the misleading ones.

fix_proposal.fix_summary: Mark each compiled table with whether something on site holds the MDI cap (the brand's mdi_primitive, or an edge at the closed-loop tier), and honour grid_cap_w in every twin replay only then. For slot-only brands, translate the cap into the max_discharge_w and floors of peak-risk discharging slots per Part 7.1 step 4, and store the demand the keyed table reaches as summary.mdi_not_enforceable, shown on the plan page.
fix_proposal.approach:
The DESIGN_LOG bullet 'every slot carries grid_cap_w so the device peak-shaves to it' holds only where something enforces the cap. At the advisory tier, v1 delivery is a person keying the table (Part 7.6), and Deye, Growatt, Sungrow, Solis and Voltronic have no such setting. Yet four replays honour the cap: plans._guard, plan_compare, demo._policy_for and verify's fidelity plan_sim. So the compare drawer and the demo's advisory figures credit peak cuts the device cannot make. The fidelity check can also call a correctly keyed table 'not applied', because the replay shaved where the device did not.

Changes:
1. compile_mode_a takes cap_enforced; plans.tick passes BRANDS[brand].mdi_primitive or tier == 'closed_loop'. The compiled table gains `mdi: {cap_kw, enforced}`. delivery.cap_enforced(compiled) reads it; a stored table without the block answers by its brand.
2. twin.slots_policy gains honour_cap (default True, so other callers are unchanged). The four replays pass cap_enforced.
3. _translate_mdi, for discharge, export and self_use slots when nothing holds the cap:
   - need = max(0, Lhi - PVlo - cap) per step. PVlo is subtracted because the MILP's MDI rows count net import with Lhi; this is logged as a deviation from the plan's max(0, Lhi - cap).
   - max_discharge_w is raised to at least the peak need (Deye keys it as its power).
   - The floor is lowered to soc_start - Σneed·0.25 h/η_d, but never below the clamp lo or the slots' reserve_pct (the floor wins).
   - Hold and charge slots are left alone: they cannot discharge on these devices.
4. _mdi_not_enforceable replays the table without the cap, adds the plan's own max(0, Lhi - L) margin (as the MILP's mdi_hi rows do), and averages per MDI block (n_mdi × 15 minutes). If the highest block is above the cap it stores {cap_kw, keyed_peak_kw, rise_kw}. It is reported, not refused: the plan says the floor wins and the rise is reported.
5. The guard and the report share one replay (plans._replay), so a tick runs no extra simulation. _guard keeps its signature plus an optional replay argument; existing tests monkeypatch it with lambda *a, **k.

Money: verify's MDI lever already prices measured peaks at real sites, so nothing there was over-credited. The honest replay fixes the demo's advisory Deye twin (Faisalabad) and the compare drawer. The web plan header shows the reached demand and a kW-only sentence, which is safe for a viewer.

Alternatives rejected:
- Dropping grid_cap_w from slot-only brands' slots: breaks the closed-loop edge contract and round 3's charge-slot cap.
- Refusing such plans in the guard: would hold every Deye plan at an MDI site.
- Capping max_charge_w on charge slots so import stays under the cap: changes the plan's energy; left to the twin-priced boundary ranking (HANDOFF 8.A.2).

fix_proposal.approach:
Shared root cause with pages-B-05: vendor_view has no translation layer (Part 7.1 step 4, DLV-02). It only renames compiled slot fields, and the web draws its columns from the row keys. The shared scaffold is given here once. pages-B-05 adds the remaining brands to the same VENDOR table and does not repeat it.

Design. Each brand function returns (rows with slot_index, settings, notes). vendor_table moves slot_index into a parallel `slots` list, so each row's keys are exactly BRANDS[brand].fields; that makes the contract API_CONTRACT.md:73 'columns = grammar.fields' true. Deye's fields gain 'program', and Huawei's become period/start/end/charge_or_discharge/days. vendor_view stays as a thin wrapper, so no caller breaks. GET /control gains vendor_slots, vendor_settings and vendor_notes. These are additive: the current web ignores them and still renders the rows.

Huawei facts come from R6 3.2, which was read for facts only; nothing from the AGPL library is copied, as Part 14 requires.
- TOU periods are charge (flag 0) or discharge (flag 1), with a days mask. Outside every period the battery does not discharge, so a hold or a solar-only charge becomes a gap. 'hold' was emitted before, and the Huawei TOU table cannot take that value.
- One grid-charge cut-off, register 47088: the highest grid-charge target.
- One discharge cut-off, register 47082: the lowest floor of the discharge periods.
- Backup SoC, register 47102: the fallback floor.
- Excess PV in TOU, register 47299: charge the battery.
- The plan's MDI cap goes in as one capacity-control period, registers 47956 on. Huawei is the only brand with mdi_primitive True. The cap is read from compiled.mdi (pages-B-03), falling back to the slots' grid_cap_w.
- The last period ends 23:59, not 00:00 (the wlcrs quirk).
- Days are 'Every day', because a day-table must be safe to repeat (Part 7.1 step 6).
Where a global register loses a per-slot value (discharge floors or grid-charge targets more than 3 points apart, the fidelity tolerance), a note says what the inverter will do instead.

Alternatives rejected:
- A hold as a 'discharge' period with floor = the hold SoC: needs per-period floors, which Huawei lacks.
- Moving grammars to delivery/brands/*.json first (DLV-00): DESIGN_LOG records the dict as the v1 form.

Not done here: the twin still replays the compiled slots, not the translated table, so the guard and the compare drawer cannot see what a translation loses. That is DLV-01's translated-table replay; meanwhile the notes make it visible.

Docs: add a DESIGN_LOG round-7 bullet. Tracker DLV-02 may stay [x] only once this lands, with the note 'register values bench_confirmed false'.

The backend hunks were applied to a scratch copy, and the translators were also run on the live compiled tables of all four demo sites. Lahore day 0 gives one charge period, the settings, and the note 'No period from 14:15 to 23:59'.

fix_proposal.approach:
Same root cause as pages-B-04: there is no per-brand translation layer, and the rows do not match grammar.fields. The scaffold, the GET /control keys (vendor_slots, vendor_settings, vendor_notes) and the web's rendering are pages-B-04's diff and are not repeated; this adds the remaining brands to its VENDOR table. Facts come from R6 3.3 and 3.4 and R8 2.15.

Sungrow (forced charging, registers 33208-33219):
- Rows: up to two forced-charge windows {window, start, end, target_soc} from the charge_grid slots, every day. The row now carries the forced-charge target; before it carried the floor (38 % where the target was 78 %).
- Set once: EMS mode Self-consumption (13050=0); forced charging enabled every day; Max SoC (13058, the highest slot target, 50-100 %); Min SoC (13059, the lowest discharging floor, capped at 50 % with a note); reserved SoC for backup (13100, the fallback floor); max charging and discharging power (33047/33048).
- Notes: a hold or a solar-only charge cannot be kept from discharging in self-consumption; a third charge window cannot be keyed.

Growatt SPH (R6 3.4):
- charge_grid, charge_pv_only and hold become Battery First windows (the battery does not discharge in Battery First). export becomes a Grid First window. discharge and self_use are Load First, the default between windows.
- Set once: charge from grid (1092), Battery First stop SoC (1091, the highest charge target), Grid First minimum SoC (1071).
- max_slots 3 becomes 6, per plan 7.1 step 2 'Growatt 3 plus 3'. A fourth window of one priority is a note; counting windows per priority belongs with HANDOFF 8.A.2's ranking.

Voltronic/Axpert: there is no time table.
- Rows are boundary changes {change, at, output_priority, charger_priority}. Output priority is SBU for discharge, self_use and export, and SUB for hold and charging. Charger priority is SNU for charge_grid, else OSO.
- Set once: a back-to-utility SoC.
- Note: each change needs a person or an edge (the emulation the plan names).

Solis:
- Rows: charge and discharge slots {kind, slot, start, end, power_w, current_a}, self-use between them.
- current_a = power / nominal_v, where nominal_v is a new optional BatteryFields field (12-1500 V) passed as battery.V_nom into compiled.battery_v. Without it the current is null and a note says to divide by the pack voltage.
- A hold cannot be keyed; the overdischarge SoC is set once.

Generic/other: fields become ['slot','start','end','mode','soc_pct'], and soc_pct keys the target on charge slots (it keyed the floor before).

All register values are bench_confirmed false (DLV-00). One test asserts list(row) == BRANDS[brand].fields for every brand, so the contract cannot drift again.

Alternatives rejected:
- Only relabelling columns: would not fix Sungrow's target or Growatt's priorities.
- Brand JSON files first (DLV-00): larger, and deferred per DESIGN_LOG.

The translators were also run on the live compiled tables. Karachi (Sungrow) day 1 gives the window 00:00-17:45 with target 82 %, Min SoC 20 % and Max SoC 82 %. The farm (Voltronic) gives one change: SBU/OSO.

title: Write-budget counter compares a UTC timestamp with a Karachi date
label: bug
steps: Closed-loop site whose edge pulls the plan between 00:00 and 05:00 PKT (19:00-24:00 UTC of the previous day). GET /sites/:id/control -> budget.used_today.
expected: Writes counted per Karachi day (the day the page and the brand's daily budget mean).
actual: `substr(sent_at,1,10) = today().isoformat()` compares store._now() (UTC ISO, store.py:106-107) with routes_common.today() (PKT date, routes_common.py:65-66), so pulls in the first five hours of a PKT day are counted on the previous day and the last five UTC hours' pulls are missed.
evidence: routes_plans.py:141-142; store.py:106; routes_common.py:65.

verdict.reason: REPRODUCED by code: routes_plans.py:141-142 `substr(sent_at,1,10) = today().isoformat()`; sent_at is written by plans._record_send (plans.py:670-673) with store._now(), which is datetime.now(timezone.utc) (store.py:106-107); routes_common.today() is datetime.now(PKT).date() (routes_common.py:65-66). So pulls between 00:00 and 05:00 PKT are dated the previous UTC day and dropped from today's count, and pulls in the last five UTC hours of the previous PKT day are counted into it. The number feeds the 'Table writes today N of M' meter on the Capabilities card (capabilities-card.tsx:19-32). Not covered by DESIGN_LOG or HANDOFF 8/9 (HANDOFF 4 'Time: UTC epoch seconds everywhere' is the convention this breaks). Could not observe live because no demo edge pulls the message (used_today reads 0 at all four sites), but the code path is unambiguous. Low as filed: the meter is informational, and a larger defect dwarfs it (each 15-minute edge pull is a plan_messages row, so at a real closed-loop site the 'writes' meter would count pulls, not table writes, and overflow the budget of 3-4 within an hour; that belongs with pages-B-02/DLV-01 rather than this timezone slip).

fix_proposal.fix_summary: Count the write-budget meter's sends between the UTC stamps that bound the Karachi day (new store.local_day_bounds) instead of comparing the UTC stamp's first ten characters with the PKT date; the same slip in the monthly report's plan-id annex (reports.py:152) is fixed with the same helper.
fix_proposal.approach: Root cause: plan_messages.sent_at is written by plans._record_send with store._now() (UTC ISO, second precision, '+00:00'), while routes_common.today() is datetime.now(PKT).date(). substr(sent_at,1,10) is the UTC date, which equals the Karachi date only from 05:00 PKT, so sends 00:00-05:00 PKT fall out of today's count and sends 19:00-24:00 UTC of the previous PKT day fall in. Fix: one helper beside store._now() (the module that defines the stamp format) returns the [lo, hi) stamps of a Karachi day in the same string form, so a range comparison on the text column is exact (every stamp has the same fixed format; microsecond stamps also sort correctly). Storage stays UTC, as HANDOFF 4 requires ('Time: UTC ... The UI shows Pakistan time'); only the day window is local. Alternatives rejected: datetime(sent_at,'+5 hours') in SQL (scatters timezone arithmetic into SQL and cannot use an index); a stored local-day column (schema change, needs a backup and migration). The same root cause is in reports.py:152 (`substr(belief_time,1,10) = d["day"]`): plan ids in the CSV annex are given the wrong local day for ticks between 19:00 and 24:00 UTC. It is fixed with the same helper. A grep finds no other `substr(...,1,10)` on a UTC stamp. Out of scope, per the verifier: the meter counts every edge pull as a 'write' (each 15-minute pull is a plan_messages row). That belongs to pages-B-02 / DLV-01's write budget. This fix keeps the day window right whichever rows are counted. All four hunks were applied to a scratch copy of the package, and the test bodies below pass there and fail on the current code.

fix_proposal.fix_summary: Give the Plan Table view a Flags column and the past 24 hours. The Flags column shows a glyph for each override kind a step lies inside, read from a new per-step `flags` list that the solver's own override masks produce. The past rows sit above the plan: each shows the plan in force at that time with the measured 15-minute values beside it, from a new GET /sites/:id/plan/past.
fix_proposal.approach:
Two gaps, one page. UI-09 (EMS_BUILD_PLAN.md:725) and R8 2.9 ask for 'SlotTable with the reason column and override glyphs, past 24 hours greyed with actuals', with a Flags column and 'actuals beside plan', refreshed every 60 s. Neither part can be built correctly in the browser from today's API.

1) Flags. plans.build_problem decides which steps an override bounds: _override_steps covers the steps overlapping [from_ts, until_ts), and build_problem builds one mask per kind. summary.overrides carries no from_ts, so the page could only guess. Fix: keep the per-kind masks on the problem as `override_kinds` and emit `flags: [kinds covering t]` on every step in _steps_out. The change is additive: optimise.shorten does not need to change, because _steps_out only reads t < T; no test asserts the exact set of step keys; delivery builds its own dicts for the edge. The web app draws one lucide glyph per kind, with sr-only words from the existing overrideWords vocabulary (the same words as the overrides list), in a Flags column after Reason as R8 places it.

2) Past rows with actuals. 'The plan in force then' needs plans.active_at's release-aware rule: no plan in force under a pause or release to native, and failed and guard-held rows skipped. Stitching versions in the browser would duplicate that rule and download up to 96 plans. Fix:
- Split active_at into active_id_at (the same SQL, returns the id only) plus a load step, so its behaviour is unchanged. The existing genset plan_requested and alert tests cover it.
- Add GET /api/sites/{id}/plan/past?hours=24 (1 to 48). For each quarter in [now-24 h, current quarter), it returns the step of the plan in force then (step dicts kept per plan id within the request) and the measured 15-minute means from telemetry.series(..., "15m"), the same source as /overview/chart: pv, load, grid, battery and genset in kW, SoC estimate else BMS, grid_present. Signs match the plan steps: battery positive is discharging, grid positive is importing. A quarter with no reading gives null, never zeros.
- The answer goes through out(), so a viewer's planned steps lose c_imp, c_exp, cost_rs and cum_rs; tests and the api walk pin this.

Web app:
- PlanViews fetches /plan/past only for the Table tab of the plan in force (not for read-only earlier versions, not for Gantt or Slots) and polls every 60 s (Part 9.3: 'now-marker and actuals 60 s').
- SlotTable merges the past rows and the plan steps by time. A past row replaces the plan's own step for the same quarter. Each past cell shows the measured figure with 'plan x' beneath it, and the reason cell says 'No plan in force' where there was none.
- The table opens scrolled to the current row, so the past is reached by scrolling up (R8).
- A 404 or error on /plan/past just leaves today's table, so the two halves can ship or roll back independently.

Alternatives rejected:
(a) Frontend only, with the actuals from /overview/chart and override windows from summary.overrides: the past rows would have no planned values, which misses the spec's point ('did the site follow the plan'), and the windows would be inexact.
(b) A stored 'executed plan' table: a schema change and more work; not needed while versions are kept 7 days.

Scope: R8's other flags (clamped by edge, budget-limited, closed-loop ack or read-back mismatch) need per-step read-back from delivery, which does not exist. This is recorded as a DESIGN_LOG deviation and in the tracker wording, rather than leaving the tracker overstating completion.

Cost: up to 96 active_id_at calls (one overrides read and one light plans read each) and at most 96 plan parses. Measure it on the Faisalabad demo, which has 122 stored versions; expect well under 0.5 s. If not, cache the answer per (site, quarter) for 60 s, or read single steps with SQLite json_extract. It is fetched only while the Table tab is open.

title: Confirmation of a marked table is computed only by the nightly job (00:40 PKT): there is no 'it took / it did not take' card, and the Mark-as-applied dialog's 'after the first peak slot' promise is not kept
label: feature-gap
steps: Advisory site: mark today's table applied at 10:00; the evening discharge slot starts 18:30. Watch the applied log and the control chip until midnight: confirmation stays 'pending' and fidelity '–'; it changes only after nightly_company (00:40 PKT) runs verify.compute_day(yesterday) which calls confirm_applied.
expected: Plan Part 9.5: 'an "it took" or "it did not take" card 30 minutes after the first peak slot'; Part 7.6 confirms 'discharge rises above 10 percent of rated within 30 minutes of a peak-slot start'; tracker UI-20 [x] names the 'it took' card.
actual: confirm_applied is reached only from verify.compute_day (verify.py:725) in the nightly job (scheduler.py:50-52); the frontend has no such card (no component mentions it); the mark-applied dialog promises 'The site's behaviour then confirms it (or not) after the first peak slot' (mark-applied.tsx:56), which is not what happens.
evidence: scheduler.py:38-52; verify.py:705-727; mark-applied.tsx:56, 84; EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md:158.

verdict.corrected_title: Confirmation of a marked table is computed only by the nightly job (00:40 PKT): there is no 'it took / it did not take' card, and the Mark-as-applied dialog's 'after the first peak slot' promise is not kept
verdict.reason: REPRODUCED in code. backend/gridlytics/verify.py:725 is the only call of confirm_applied, inside compute_day; compute_day is reached from scheduler.nightly_company (scheduler.py:38-52, yesterday only), demo.py:285 (the seed), and verify.compute_range from POST /api/sites/:id/savings/recompute (routes_savings.py:46-56, permission run_jobs, default end = yesterday; a caller would have to pass end=today and it still classifies the whole day). plans.py:654 writes confirmation 'pending' on apply. routes_sites.py:49-52 control_state flips the chip to 'Following plan (table applied)' as soon as an applied row exists for today, before any telemetry evidence. alerts.py:75-98 _peak_unconfirmed raises apply_unconfirmed 30 min after the first peak step only when NO mark exists; it is not a took/did-not-take verdict of a marked table. Frontend grep for 'it took'/'did not take'/'took card' across frontend/src: nothing; the applied log (mark-applied.tsx:95-118) shows the stored 'pending'; mark-applied.tsx:56 tells the user 'The site's behaviour then confirms it (or not) after the first peak slot'; savings-days-table.tsx:11 shows 'Awaiting confirmation'. Live control answer for 6d4db49bf87e: applied [] (demo), so a live walk could not be done without writing to the shared demo. Spec: EMS_BUILD_PLAN.md:751 (Part 9.5, the 'it took' or 'it did not take' card 30 minutes after the first peak slot), :637 (Part 7.6 boundary test within 30 minutes), tracker EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md:158 UI-20 [x] names the card. BY-DESIGN: DESIGN_LOG 'Savings: Advisory confirmation needs evidence ... a simplified form of Part 7.6' (lines 217-219) documents the simplified classification, not that it only runs nightly; HANDOFF 8 and 9 do not list it. Medium: the installer's promised feedback flow is missing and the dialog sentence is misleading; money is not wrong because the savings gate still withholds the claim until 'confirmed'.

fix_proposal.fix_summary: Compute the early 'it took / it did not take' verdict for today's marked table in the 15-minute tick, 30 minutes after its first discharge slot in the peak. Keep it on the applied row (`early_check`), show it as a card on Devices and control, raise a Control alert when it did not take, and make the Mark-as-applied dialog say what really happens. The nightly confirm_applied keeps deciding the day's class and the claim.
fix_proposal.approach:
Root cause: verify.confirm_applied runs only inside verify.compute_day, which is reached from the nightly job (yesterday), the demo seed and the manual recompute (default end = yesterday). Nothing reads a marked table during the day, so the card that plan 9.5 and tracker UI-20 [x] promise never exists. The dialog sentence (mark-applied.tsx:56) promises a check after the first peak slot that does not happen.

Fix: add `verify.first_peak_check(site_id, now, site)`. It takes today's latest applied row and the plan the row names, then finds the first boundary into a discharge or export slot that starts in the connection's peak window. At a site with no TOU window it takes any discharge start. The slot must start no earlier than one quarter before the mark, because a table cannot be followed before it is keyed. Before boundary + 30 minutes the verdict is 'waiting', with `due_ts`. After that it applies confirm_applied's own boundary test (discharge above 10 % of rated within 30 minutes, grid present). Two guards stop the test from crediting what the native settings would have done anyway:
- It replays the table and the native capture in force through the twin from the measured SoC over the hour round the start. If the table would not discharge there either (the battery near its floor), the verdict is 'no_evidence'.
- If native would discharge too, the measured energy over the hour must be closer to one replay than the other by 2 % of the battery. This is the same margin as the nightly 'not_applied' rule.
If there are fewer than 10 battery readings in the window, the verdict stays 'waiting' (reason no_battery_power), because a CSV site uploads later. A final verdict (took, did_not_take, no_evidence, no_peak_slot) is stored once in applied.data.early_check and never recomputed. _record_confirmation merges into the same data dict, so the nightly run keeps it.

Where it runs:
- alerts.evaluate runs it each tick for advisory sites with a plan, demo sites included, so the demo shows the card. It raises a Control warning 'apply_did_not_take', gated like the other Control alerts by `settled` and never at demo sites.
- POST /plan/apply runs it once for a mark made for today, so the card appears at once.
- plans.applied_rows returns `early_check`, and the web app shows a TookCard above Mark as applied.

Money: nothing changes. `confirmation`, fidelity and the claim are still written only by the nightly confirm_applied, so the savings gate (DLV-05) is untouched. This respects DESIGN_LOG 'Advisory confirmation needs evidence' (no verdict without battery power or a distinguishable test). The DESIGN_LOG entry records that this is one boundary only, a simplified Part 7.6.

Alternatives considered:
- Calling confirm_applied on a partial day: it writes `confirmation` and would gate money on a half-day.
- Moving the whole nightly job earlier: still not 30 minutes after the slot.
- Wording-only (change the dialog to 'overnight'): this fixes the misleading sentence, but UI-20 [x] and plan 9.5 would still be false.

Shared context with pages-B-02: both are gaps in the advisory tier's keyed-table cycle (issue, key, mark, confirm). After B-02 the mark names the issued table's plan, which is what this check replays. The fixes are independent and touch different hunks of the same files.

Validated: the backend edits compile, and test_fix_r7_early_check.py passes when run by hand against a patched scratch copy. The full diffs are /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f64857cc-0ca7-5cbb-b665-d2b474fb2fb8/scratchpad/audit/r7fix/per/B-08.backend.diff and B-08.frontend.diff.

fix_proposal.fix_summary: Make the Plan and Overview first-plan checklists count the grid step done by the API's own rule (a connection, a farm, or data.off_grid). Do it with one shared gridSettled helper, which canRemoveConnection also uses, so the three copies of the rule cannot drift apart again.
fix_proposal.approach:
Root cause: the rule 'tab C is complete' exists in three copies in the web app. plan-empty.tsx:11 and overview-page.tsx:78 use `connections.length || site_type === "farm"`. site-form.ts:292 canRemoveConnection already adds data.off_grid. The backend has one rule, routes_sites._grid_settled (line 171), which POST /activate and DELETE /connection apply: `bool(connections) or site_type == "farm" or data.off_grid`. BACKEND_ASKS.md:65 records 'activate counts data.off_grid', and DESIGN_LOG round 3 line 128 says SiteFields carries off_grid on any site type.

Fix: one display-side mirror, `gridSettled(site, connections?)`, in a new frontend/src/lib/site-rules.ts. It imports no zod, so the plan and overview chunks do not pull in site-form's schemas. PlanEmpty, the Overview Checklist and canRemoveConnection all call it. HANDOFF section 5 says 'the server is the authority': this helper only decides how the page words the step and refuses nothing.

Alternatives considered:
(a) Add `|| site.data.off_grid` to the two checklist lines. This fixes the symptom but keeps three copies of the rule.
(b) Ask the backend for a `grid_settled` or `checklist` field on GET /sites/:id. This is the cleanest single source, but it needs a backend round and a contract change for a low-severity issue. It is a fine follow-up and would replace gridSettled.

Left unchanged on purpose: the verifier's aside that a grid-connected farm shows 'Done' before its connection is saved. That is the backend's own rule (_grid_settled counts every farm as settled, so activate accepts it). The pages keep parity with it. If the owner wants a grid-connected farm (wizard farm_grid true) to need its connection, change _grid_settled and gridSettled together, for example 'a farm counts only when data.off_grid is not False'. Raise that as an owner question, not part of this fix.

title: Compare drawer silently compares against an assumed self-use baseline when no native capture exists
label: ux
steps: Site with a battery and a plan but no native capture (common at monitor before capture). Open 'Compare with native': the table shows figures for 'Native settings' with the method note 'the native arm the captured native settings'.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in code. routes_plans.py:106-128 plan_compare returns {compare: None} only when there is no plan or no battery. Otherwise it runs twin.native_policy, which at twin.py:167 falls back to {work_mode: self_use, backup_soc_pct: 20, slots: []} when site.native is missing. Plans are solved for any active site (scheduler.tick_company). A capture is required only for a tier above monitor (routes_sites.py:315), so a monitor-tier site with a battery and no capture gets a comparison. compare-drawer.tsx:38-41 and 69-72 never check for a capture: it labels the column 'Native settings' and says 'the native arm the captured native settings', and owners and analysts see an energy-cost difference row. Spec: R8-ux-pages.md:354 says the Compare drawer is 'disabled with "Needs the native-settings capture and 1 day of data"'. The tracker's UI-09 cites R8 2.9, and DESIGN_LOG has no contrary decision. I could not reproduce it live: all four demo sites have captures (checked via /api/sites/:id), and I did not create a site because that would change app state. It is medium rather than low because it shows rupee figures against an assumed baseline labelled as captured, which misleads at exactly the pre-control sales stage.

fix_proposal.fix_summary: Gate the compare drawer as R8 2.9 asks. GET /plan/compare answers {compare: null, reason: no_capture | too_little_data} until the native settings are captured and a day of data exists, and the web app disables 'Compare with native' with 'Needs the native-settings capture and 1 day of data'. The method note names the capture version that is replayed.
fix_proposal.approach:
Root cause: routes_plans.plan_compare (lines 106-128) checks only for a plan and a battery. It then replays twin.native_policy, which falls back to self-use with a 20 % floor when site.native is missing (twin.py:167). Plans are solved for every active site, but a capture is required only above the monitor tier (routes_sites.py:315). So a monitor site with a battery and no capture gets rupee figures against an assumed baseline that compare-drawer.tsx labels 'Native settings' / 'the captured native settings'. That is exactly the pre-control sales stage.

Fix (backend): return {compare: null, reason} for no_plan, no_battery, no_capture (s['native'] empty), or too_little_data (telemetry.first_ts younger than 86,400 s, the R8 '1 day of data'). Add `native: {version, captured_at}` to a real comparison.

Fix (frontend):
- CompareButton takes hasCapture from the site query the plan page already loads. When it is false the button is disabled and COMPARE_NEEDS is shown beside it, as R8 asks.
- CompareBody explains each `reason`, in case the site answer is stale.
- The method note names the capture version and date.

The gate goes on the server as well as the button, so no reader (API key, report, older page) gets a comparison labelled 'captured' that is really a guess. twin.native_policy's fallback stays, because the savings replay (verify.compute_day) needs it for monitor-tier recommendation-only days, which claim nothing.

Alternatives considered:
- Relabelling the arm 'Assumed self-use (no capture)': rejected because R8 2.9 says disabled, and an assumed baseline in rupees misleads at sale time.
- Gating only in the web app: rejected because the API stays wrong.

Validated: the backend edits compile; test_fix_r7_compare.py passes when run by hand on a patched scratch copy; and tsc --noEmit passes on the patched web app. The full diffs are /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f64857cc-0ca7-5cbb-b665-d2b474fb2fb8/scratchpad/audit/r7fix/per/B-14.backend.diff and B-14.frontend.diff.

label: ux

verdict.reason: Confirmed. control-actions.tsx:31-34 (release) says 'the plan keeps solving as a recommendation'. The pause text at lines 35-38, and plan-held.tsx:45-49, say 'no plan is in force ... keeps each plan for reading, marked held'. The backend at plans.py:452-455 stores the plan as status 'held' while a release is in force. DESIGN_LOG.md:184-185 settles that while a pause or release is in force 'no plan is in force ... A tick stores its plan as held'. So the release dialog contradicts the settled rule and the Plan page. 'Recommendation' is the monitor-tier word, which could lead an operator to expect a table to key in. The impact is wording only, so the severity is low.

fix_proposal.fix_summary: Make the Release-to-native dialog (and the Pause dialog, and the Plan page's held card) use one shared sentence, NO_PLAN_IN_FORCE: no plan is in force, and the optimiser keeps each plan for reading, marked held. Drop 'the plan keeps solving as a recommendation', and correct the monitor-tier note.
fix_proposal.approach:
Root cause: the release copy in control-actions.tsx:33 was written before the round-1/2 decision in DESIGN_LOG ('Pause and release to native: while either is in force, no plan is in force ... A tick stores its plan as held'). plans.tick stores a held plan under a release (plans.py:452-455), and plan-held.tsx says so, but the dialog still uses the monitor-tier word 'recommendation' (plan 9.4). That can lead an operator at an advisory site to expect a table to key in.

The new series are grid import and export energy, battery voltage, current and SoH, SoC sigma, genset running, grid frequency, unserved load and curtailed PV. fix_proposal.approach:
This is a web-app-only gap. GET /sites/:id/telemetry already answers any name in telemetry.NUMERIC; the verifier's live call returned 200 with these names. The picker's fixed list (telemetry-series.ts:18-30) is the only limit. - kW series (curtail_w, unserved_w) go on the main left axis.
- % series (SoH) go on the right axis.
- battery_soc_sigma_pct is not a line of its own. It becomes a ±1 sigma band around the SoC estimate, using TimeSeriesChart's existing `band` support (R8: 'SoC estimate with sigma band').
- Flags become shaded bands: gridBands is generalised to flagBands with 'down' (grid_present, as today) and 'on' (genset_running, where the bucket's share running is above 0).
- Energy series (grid_import_wh, grid_export_wh) are SUMmed per bucket by the API (telemetry.SERIES_KIND), so they are drawn as kWh-per-bucket bars in their own small chart, titled with the resolution ('kWh per 15 minutes'). That avoids implying a rate.
- V, A, Hz, °C and L series get their own small charts, as voltage does today.

The picker becomes five fieldsets with legends, one per group. Each is an accessible group; checkbox names are unchanged, so the existing tests still find them.

Ranges:
- 'today' runs from 00:00 Karachi to now. It is live and polled every 60 s, with its end at least a minute after midnight so the API never refuses an empty range.
- 'yesterday' is the whole previous Karachi day and is static.
- Both are cached by their day (rangeDays), so they are fetched afresh after midnight.
- rangeIncludesNow becomes simply 'end >= now', which is correct for every key.

Left out, and recorded in API_CONTRACT: export_limit_active_w, censored and quality_flags (diagnostics, not in R8's list); per-string PV and the derived series (net load, self-consumption %), which need new API work; and R8's 'up to 8 series' cap, which is not enforced today. fix_proposal.fix_summary: Implement plan Part 9.3 in local sign-in: a company administrator (manage_users) issues a one-time password that must be changed at the next sign-in and clears a sign-in lockout, the founder console does the same across companies, and the sign-in text tells people who to ask.
fix_proposal.approach:
Corrected title: Sign-in tells people to ask their company admin for a new password, but only the founder console can set one; there is no forced first-sign-in change and no lockout clearing (medium).

Why this fix. The plan says two things. D4 (EMS_BUILD_PLAN.md:42) and the platform paragraph (:218) put password resets in the founder console 'until email exists'. Part 9.3's last paragraph (:736) is later and more specific: 'an admin issues a one-time password with a forced change on first sign-in and can clear a lockout, the founder console does the same across companies, and the Forgot password text says to ask the company's admin'. login-page.tsx:71 already follows 9.3, but the backend never gave an admin the means. The fix builds the missing pieces so the sign-in text becomes true. It records the D4/9.3 conflict and the choice in DESIGN_LOG; nothing there covers it today.

Alternative considered: copy only. Change login-page.tsx:71 to 'Ask us (OnyxLeaf) for a new one', as Solarlytics' Login.tsx:69 does, and leave resets to the founder. That is a 1-line S change that matches D4, but it keeps the plan's forced change and lockout clearing missing, and it makes OnyxLeaf a help desk for every forgotten password in every company. If the owner prefers D4, apply only the login-page.tsx line, with the text 'Ask us (OnyxLeaf) for a new one', and drop the rest.

Design (local mode only; Supabase mode keeps its own email resets):
1. platform.db schema 2 adds accounts.must_change. _connect() already copies the file to backup/ before any migration, so the rule 'back up before schema changes' holds. platform.set_password(..., temporary=True) sets the flag, and any other set clears it; the person's own /api/local/password change is such a set, so no change is needed in routes_local.
2. companies._local_context refuses with 403 password_change_required while the flag is set. The guard sends every request through companies.resolve except IDENTITY_PATHS (/api/local/context, /api/local/password, logout, refresh), so the person can read their context and change the password and nothing else. /api/auth/state carries the refusal instead of failing. The session answer's `user` is unchanged, because test_platform.py:265 pins it; the flag reaches the web app as context.profile.must_change_password.
3. Lockout clearing: a LOCK_CLEARED event in account_events. lock_wait counts refusals only after max(last good sign-in from the address, last clear from any address). It is the same mechanism as R-235's 'a good sign-in clears the count', with no new table.
4. New routes beside PUT /api/users/{id} in api.py; routes_platform stays 'org and keys only' per Part 10.4 step 4. POST /api/users/{id}/password generates a 19-character password from 31 letters that cannot be confused when read out, about 79 bits. It sets the password with temporary=True, which ends every session, clears the lockout, and answers the password once. It never goes into an audit line, and the company audit says 'issued a one-time password'. POST /api/users/{id}/unlock clears the lockout.
5. Guard rails, which the plan does not spell out and which are needed for tenant safety: manage_users only; never oneself (My account does that); never the owner (OnyxLeaf resets the owner's); never an account that also has a membership in another company, because an admin of company A must not take over the person's access to company B. The members table already pins the owner the same way.
6. Founder console: the password route takes an optional boolean `temporary` (in local mode it also clears the lockout), and a new POST /api/founder/users/{id}/unlock. Both are audited in founder_audit. Supabase mode answers 409 not_local_mode.
7. Web app: the routing state gets 'must-change', and RequireActiveMembership shows only the lifted PasswordForm. changePassword re-reads the context afterwards, so the app opens. Members gets a 'Sign-in help' dialog with 'Clear the lockout' and 'Issue a one-time password' (shown once, selectable). The founder console's Set a password gets a checkbox, ticked by default, and a Clear lockout button. The login text names the owner exception.
Owner's constraints are kept: no self-signup, no Google or social sign-in, no email; accounts stay preassigned by the founder, and the admin only helps an existing member back in.

Related inconsistency: a connection with regime off_grid shows its tariff_category in the header but 'Off-grid' in Fleet. Not reproduced live: every demo site has its connection. Only an unactivated site can be in this state: activation needs _grid_settled (routes_sites.py:170-187), and removing the last connection of an active site is refused (:256). fix_proposal.fix_summary: Treat off-grid as a property of the site (a connection of regime off_grid, or no connection at a farm or a site flagged off_grid), so a grid site whose tab C is not saved yet reads "no connection yet" in the site header and has a null category in the Fleet, and its outages count.
fix_proposal.approach:
Corrected title: A grid site whose connection is not saved yet is labelled "Off-grid" in the site header and the Fleet table (low).

Root cause, shared by both places: 'no saved connection' is used as a stand-in for 'off-grid'. site-header.tsx:35 prints ' · Off-grid' whenever connections[0] is missing. routes_sites.fleet_row:90-92 sets category 'Off-grid' when conn is None, and the summary's in_outage (:106) and fleetKpis (fleet-page.tsx:49) then leave such a site out. The backend already has the right rule in _grid_settled (routes_sites.py:171-175): a farm or data.off_grid without a connection is off-grid. A connection is off-grid by its regime. The fix reuses it: `conn regime == off_grid if conn else _grid_settled(s, [])`. This gives one definition on the server and the same three-part rule in one exported frontend helper (gridWords), so the header, the Fleet and tab C agree.

The category stays a display string ('Off-grid' or the tariff category), as the contract has it, so fleetKpis and the in_outage comparison keep working. Only the unset case becomes null, and the page shows it as 'no connection yet'. The related inconsistency the verifier noted is fixed too: a connection of regime off_grid now reads 'Off-grid' in the header, as it already did in the Fleet.

Alternatives considered: (a) a new `grid` enum field ('on'|'off'|'unset') on the fleet row. It is cleaner, but every consumer would change and the contract would gain a field; null on the existing field is enough. (b) Hiding unactivated sites from Fleet. That is wrong: R8 2.1 wants new sites listed with 'Collecting data'. plans.py:171 also treats conn None as off-grid, but only active sites are planned, and activation needs _grid_settled, so planning is not affected. No DESIGN_LOG rule touches this.

fix_proposal.approach:
The decision is documented: DESIGN_LOG 2026-11-06 'Demo (Part 9.6)' sets 21 days, with GRIDLYTICS_DEMO_DAYS, against the plan's 90, and HANDOFF 9.1 agrees. Only the copy kept the plan's number (fleet-page.tsx:116, demo-tab.tsx:34). Hard-coding '21' would go wrong again whenever GRIDLYTICS_DEMO_DAYS is set; this scratch seed has 14, and the live GET /api/demo answered 56 of 56 for four sites. So the backend states the figure: demo.load records `days` in the status, and GET /api/demo answers `days`. That value is the build's own, else total divided by the number of demo sites for a status written before this change, else what a load would build now (default_days()). The pages read it, and with no answer they say 'simulated history' with no number, never a wrong one.

Alternative considered: a frontend-only edit removing the number ('with simulated history'). It costs no backend change, but loses information R8 2.18 thought worth stating; it is acceptable as a hotfix.

The empty state becomes a small NoSites component so the hook is not called inside QueryState's render callback. pages-A-17 adds the product statement to the same component. No plan text changes: the plan keeps 90 as the target, and DESIGN_LOG already records the deviation.

fix_proposal.fix_summary: Bring UI-01 Fleet up to R8 2.1. Add 'On a plan' and litres-avoided tiles. Add DISCO, tier, control-state and genset filters. Draw the battery direction and genset on/off in the Now glyph. Show 'First plan after tariff and assets are confirmed' and 'Collecting data: 0 of 14 days'. Add an owner and admin row menu (Open settings, Release to native, Pause writes) and the one-line product statement on the no-sites page.
fix_proposal.approach:
These are real gaps against the spec (EMS_BUILD_PLAN.md:717 and :984 UI-01, citing R8 2.1, and R8 2.19 step 1) although EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS marks UI-01 [x]. Each is small, so the fix is a set of small changes, each traceable to an R8 2.1 clause:

1. Now glyph. The fleet row's `now` already carries battery_kw, genset_kw and genset_running (routes_sites._snapshot:61-63, confirmed live: Karachi battery_kw -22.24 while charging). Only the page and the contract line ignore them, so this part is frontend only. Signs follow OpenEMS, as telemetry.py:3 states: discharge positive. A null genset signal at a site with a genset reads 'Genset: no signal', following UI-11's rule that a missing signal is unknown, not off.
2. Summary strip. R8 asks for sites on a plan, sites on native mode, MTD Rs and litres avoided. The backend adds `on_plan` (a plan exists and control is not paused or released), `has_genset` and `mtd_litres_saved` to each row, and `on_plan` and `mtd_litres_saved` to the summary. The litres are summed from the ledger's per-day litres_saved, as the Savings page does (verify.py:1055). Litres are not money: no key is in money.MONEY_KEYS and none ends in _rs, so a viewer sees them, as R8 2.1 asks ('kWh shifted and litres instead'). 'On native settings' is shown as the complement in the 'On a plan' sub-line rather than as a seventh tile. The existing useful tiles (Sites online, Open alerts, In an outage now) stay; KpiRow takes 6 on xl.
3. Filters. R8 lists DISCO, tier, state and has genset. They are added as four selects beside the existing segmented quick filter and search, computed client-side from the fleet answer, which is one round trip as R8 wants.
4. Next event. 'First plan after tariff and assets are confirmed' shows for a site that is not active (new sites are created 'observing', sites.py:221). An active site with no plan yet keeps 'No plan yet', and the existing released or paused text stays.
5. Collecting data. routes_sites.py:95 returns collecting_day 0 for a site with no telemetry, but the page's truthy check hid it. The check becomes `!= null`, with R8's own words 'Collecting data: 0 of 14 days'.
6. Row menu. R8 asks for the owner's kebab (pause control, release, open settings). It reuses the Devices and control page's own confirmation dialog, by exporting ActionDialog from control-actions.tsx, with the same permissions (hold_release for release, resume_control for pause), and it also invalidates the fleet query. It is shown only to roles that hold one of those permissions. The dropdown uses the same Radix menu and classes as top-bar.tsx, which keeps the Boxlytics look.
7. No-sites page. It gets R8 2.19's one-line statement (plans and verifies, never starts a genset itself, starts in monitor). It is added to the NoSites component that pages-A-04 introduces. The wording avoids the banned words of source-rules.test.ts.
Out of scope: the map toggle ('later' in the plan) and the one-site redirect, which this finding does not cover. Update EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS's UI-01 note when it lands. The diffs assume pages-A-03's and pages-A-04's changes are already applied, since they touch the same file and type.
