title: API_CONTRACT states the wear cost as replacement / (2 x cycles x depth); the page and optimise.wear_cost divide by cycles x depth
label: spec-mismatch
steps: Compare docs/API_CONTRACT.md:237 with site-form.ts:297-300 (`replacement_cost_per_kwh / (warranted_cycles * warranted_depth)`, "per kWh discharged") and backend optimise.py:968-970 (same formula).
expected: The contract describes what the page computes.
actual: The doc keeps an older "per kWh of throughput" formula with a factor 2 that the code does not use; a reader checking the tile against the doc would think the page is double.
evidence: API_CONTRACT.md:237; site-form.ts:297-300; optimise.py:968-970; new-site-page.test.tsx:82 asserts 10.8333 for 52000/(6000x0.8).

verdict.reason: Confirmed. API_CONTRACT.md:237 still says 'wear cost per kWh of throughput = replacement_cost_per_kwh / (2 x warranted_cycles x warranted_depth)'. The code divides by cycles x depth only, per kWh discharged: site-form.ts:295-300 wearCostPerKwh and backend optimise.py:968-970 wear_cost. new-site-page.test.tsx:82 expects 10.8333 for 52000/(6000x0.8). BUILD_NOTES.md:56-57 records the round-3 fix ('the wear cost is per kWh discharged (it was half the optimiser's)'), and the contract line was never updated. The stale line is in docs only; the page shows the right figure. It could still mislead someone checking money figures against the doc, so low.

fix_proposal.fix_summary: Correct docs/API_CONTRACT.md:237 to the wear cost the page and the optimiser compute: replacement_cost_per_kwh / (warranted_cycles x warranted_depth), per kWh discharged, with the golden figure, and pin it with a doc test.
fix_proposal.approach:
This is a documentation and spec mismatch, so the change goes in the doc. The code is right and already pinned: site-form.ts:295-300 wearCostPerKwh equals optimise.wear_cost (optimise.py:968-970), which battery.py:25 and plans.py:262 use as c_cyc, and new-site-page.test.tsx:82 asserts 10.8333 for 52000/(6000x0.8). The round-3 fix in BUILD_NOTES.md:56-57 ('the wear cost is per kWh discharged (it was half the optimiser's)') changed the code but left the contract line with the old '2 x' throughput convention. The plan's own figures (EMS_BUILD_PLAN.md:374: 'Rs 9.4 to 13.5 if the warranty's 80 percent depth is honoured') match the code's cycles x depth convention, so neither the code nor the plan changes.

The money rule ('every money calculation gets a golden test') is already met in code. The only test to add is a small node-env vitest in the source-rules style. It fails if the contract states the formula differently from the code again, so the doc cannot drift silently. Alternative: no test, doc edit only. Rejected, because the drift came back once already.

changes.diff:
```diff
@@ (UI-02, line 237)
-Derived on the page: the battery's wear cost per kWh of throughput = `replacement_cost_per_kwh / (2 x warranted_cycles x warranted_depth)` (see_costs only).
+Derived on the page: the battery's wear cost per kWh discharged = `replacement_cost_per_kwh / (warranted_cycles x warranted_depth)` (see_costs only), the
+figure the optimiser charges (`optimise.wear_cost`, the Battery page's `c_cyc`) and `site-form.ts` `wearCostPerKwh` computes; golden: 52,000 / (6,000 x 0.8)
+= Rs 10.83 per kWh discharged.
```

fix_proposal.risk: None at runtime: the change is to a document plus one test. Roll-back: revert the commit.

title: Fee card labels a whole-month extrapolation of the claim 'Verified saving a month', names the wrong baseline, and never shows the basis or a Preliminary mark
label: bug
steps: As admin on a site with a few priced days in the current billing month (e.g. 3 confirmed days claiming Rs 5,000 each), open /sites/:id/savings. Read the Fee check card.
expected: The card shows a saving that was actually verified in the period, says it is the smaller of the two baselines, and, if any scaling to a month is done, says so beside the figure (plan 9.7: every money figure with its method; plan 8.4: never over-claim).
actual: verify.summary scales the claimed rupees per scored day to the whole billing month (`c / n * dim + mdi_c`, line 1113), takes the smaller baseline and averages months, then labels it `verified_saving_rs_per_month`. The FeeCard (fee-card.tsx lines 40-43) prints it as 'Verified saving a month' with the subtitle 'claimed against the native settings, per month in the period' (wrong on both counts: it is the min of native and tuned, and it is extrapolated) and never shows `fee.basis`. The verdict badge 'Fee within one third of the verified saving' can therefore be green on three days of data.
evidence: verify.py 1105-1119 (`basis` string documents the scaling but is only in the JSON); frontend/src/features/savings/fee-card.tsx 37-43 reads `fee.fee_rs_per_month`, `fee.verified_saving_rs_per_month`, `fee.within_one_third` only; `Savings['fee']` type (types/api.ts 816) has no `basis`.

verdict.corrected_title: Fee card labels a whole-month extrapolation of the claim 'Verified saving a month', names the wrong baseline, and never shows the basis or a Preliminary mark
verdict.reason: REPRODUCED. verify.py 1105-1119: per month, c/n*dim + mdi_c where c = claimed Rs, n = days that could claim (m[5]), dim = billing-month days; min over native/tuned; months averaged. Live GET /api/sites/47895916bed4/savings (owner, period 1-9 Nov): native claimed_rs 12,580.84 over 8 days -> fee.verified_saving_rs_per_month 47,178 (= 12,581/8*30); screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f64857cc-0ca7-5cbb-b665-d2b474fb2fb8/scratchpad/audit/verify-pagesD/owner-1440-sites_47895916bed4_savings.png shows 'Verified saving a month Rs 47,178 / claimed against the native settings, per month in the period' under a tile saying 'Claimed on verified days: Rs 12,581'. Faisalabad (6d4db49bf87e): 1 confirmed day; fee tile Rs 1,719 is the tuned extrapolation (458.32/8*30) while the subtitle says 'against the native settings' (native would be 7,129) - screenshot owner-1440-sites_6d4db49bf87e_savings.png. fee-card.tsx 37-43 reads only fee_rs_per_month/verified_saving_rs_per_month/within_one_third; types/api.ts Savings['fee'] has no basis; the FeeCard KpiTiles pass no `preliminary` prop. within_one_third = fee <= saving_pm/3 (line 1117), so with a fee set it is green on a few scored days. BY-DESIGN check: the scaling itself IS a deliberate, tested decision (code comment 'a part month is not a month'; test_fix_r2_savings.py:300-320 'regression-fee-rate-counts-withheld-days' asserts 10 claiming days of Rs 1,000 -> 30,000 a month), and it is reasonable for comparing a monthly fee, so design_wrong=false and the extrapolation per se is not the defect. No DESIGN_LOG/HANDOFF 8-9 entry covers the label. What remains is a real defect: plan 9.7 ('every money figure with its method'; 'Verified' only when the method is complete) and Part 8's own rule (price against verified savings) are broken by calling a 3.75x extrapolation 'Verified', naming the wrong baseline and hiding `basis`. High: a misleading savings figure in the pricing card, visible to the admin/analyst who sets the fee, contradicting the claimed figure on the same page.

title: Headline 'Saving against the native settings' is the all-days sum, including days that claim nothing
label: spec-mismatch
area: Savings / KPI tiles, ledger, monthly PDF
steps: Open /sites/:id/savings as admin at an advisory site where several days are 'Not applied', 'Awaiting confirmation' or 'Claim withheld'. Compare the big figure of the first tile with the small 'Claimed on verified days' line; do the same for the ledger's bold 'Saving, all days' row and the PDF headline.
expected: The headline money figure is the claim (plan 8.4: a 'not applied' day claims nothing; fidelity gates), with the unclaimed all-days figure, if shown at all, subordinate and explained; R8 2.12's headline ledger is the saving the product stands behind.
actual: verify.summary sums `d['saving_rs']` over every day regardless of fidelity or withheld claim (line 1053) and adds the month MDI lever (1078); savings-kpis.tsx puts that `saving_rs` in the tile's large value with `claimed_rs` as a subtitle; savings-ledger.tsx 76-85 bolds 'Saving, all days' and shows 'Claimed' as a plain row; reports.py 115-119 prints 'Saving' before 'Claimed (applied days)'. At a monitor-tier site (the demo mall) the headline is the noise of actual-vs-native replay presented as a saving.
evidence: verify.py 1050-1053, 1078; savings-kpis.tsx 32-33; savings-ledger.tsx 76-85; reports.py 115-119; fleet route also exposes both (routes_savings.py 203).

verdict.reason: REPRODUCED. verify.py 1051-1053 sums d['saving_rs'] over every day (any fidelity, withheld or not) and 1078 adds the month MDI; savings-kpis.tsx 32-33 puts saving_rs in the big value with claimed_rs as a subtitle on the native tile only (the tuned tile, lines 34-35, has no claimed line at all); savings-ledger.tsx 76-85 bolds 'Saving, all days' over a plain 'Claimed (verified days only)'; reports.py 115-119 prints 'Saving' before 'Claimed (applied days)'. Live: Faisalabad (7 native_block days + 1 confirmed) shows tuned tile '-Rs 1,919' while the claim against tuned is +Rs 458 (screenshot .../verify-pagesD/owner-1440-sites_6d4db49bf87e_savings.png); Lahore monitor-tier mall (8 recommendation_only days) shows 'Saving against a tuned table -Rs 1,239' with 'Claimed Rs 0' (owner-1440-sites_37b2fd882dcb_savings.png). Extra evidence: the fleet page's 'Saving this month' sums claimed_rs (routes_sites.py _mtd_saving, 'mtd += d.get("claimed_rs")'), so Fleet and Savings disagree on the same month. BY-DESIGN: DESIGN_LOG (v1 build, Savings) says 'a day claims its saving only when its fidelity is confirmed' and the mall 'shows no claimed saving, honestly' - the documented honest figure is the claim; nothing documents making the all-days replay the headline. Plan 8.4 ('not applied claims nothing') and 8.5 ('headline saving against each baseline') support the finding. Medium: misleading figures (both directions) on the proof page and PDF, not an over-claimed invoice.

title: MDI lever is taken from month-to-date peaks on the default 'This month' period and shown without a provisional/full-month label (95 % of Karachi's headline claim on day 9)
label: spec-mismatch
steps: Mid-month, open /sites/:id/savings (default period 'This month') at an MDI-billed site (B-2/B-3). Read the 'Maximum demand (MDI)' lever row and the tile headline; then confirm one day's table applied and recompute.
expected: Plan 8.2: MDI is the month's single highest block, so the lever comes 'from the full-month counterfactual only, labelled as such'; a partial month's MDI difference is provisional and should be marked, and a month's MDI lever should not be claimed on the strength of one claiming day.
actual: `mdi_by_month` uses the max peaks of whatever days fall in the period (lines 1061-1073), adds it to `saving_rs` for every month touched, and adds it to `claimed_rs` whenever `months[k][3] > 0`, i.e. one confirmed/partial day in the month (1075). The ledger row (levers.ts line 12) and the 'Maximum demand by month' list (savings-ledger.tsx 10-18) carry no provisional/partial-month mark. Period is calendar-month while MDI rows are keyed by billing month (`bill_month`), so with a `reading_day` connection the listed month key can span outside the chosen period.
evidence: verify.py 1061-1078; levers.ts 12; savings-ledger.tsx 101-105; period.ts 22-31 (no billing-period option).

verdict.corrected_title: MDI lever is taken from month-to-date peaks on the default 'This month' period and shown without a provisional/full-month label (95 % of Karachi's headline claim on day 9)
verdict.reason: REPRODUCED. verify.py 1058-1078: months[bill_month] keeps max actual/baseline peak over whatever days are in the period; mdi_by_month = (max(floor, baseline) - max(floor, actual)) * rate; added to saving_rs for every month and to claimed_rs whenever months[k][3] > 0 (one confirmed/partial day). Live GET /api/sites/e9941b41c70b/savings (owner, 1-9 Nov, 8 of 30 days): levers.mdi 41,637.5 (902.0 vs 935.3 kW), claimed_rs 43,593.81, i.e. the MDI lever is 95 % of the headline claim; screenshot .../verify-pagesD/owner-1440-sites_e9941b41c70b_savings.png shows 'Maximum demand (MDI) Rs 41,638' and 'Maximum demand by month 2026-11: 902 kW actual, 935 kW baseline' with no to-date mark; levers.ts 12 and savings-ledger.tsx 10-18 carry no such label (grep 'to date|provisional|full-month' in features/savings: nothing); only the generic Preliminary badge on the tiles. period.ts 22-31 has no billing-period option; bill_month keys by tariffs.billing_month_for (reading_day) - code-confirmed, not live-reproducible since no demo connection has a reading_day. BY-DESIGN: DESIGN_LOG says only 'MDI is a monthly lever from the arms' monthly peaks'; plan 8.2 wants it 'from the full-month counterfactual only, labelled as such'; HANDOFF 8-9 do not list it. The 'one claiming day' objection is weaker (the MDI is by nature the month's single block), so the keepable defect is the unlabelled partial-month lever. Medium: misleading figure mid-month, resolves at month end.

title: PUT /sites/:id/pilot has no request model: it stores any JSON for the pilot fields and lets the client write the signoff record (and, before start, forge amendments); a null criteria crashes the pilot page
label: bug
steps: As admin, after POST /pilot/start, send PUT /api/sites/:id/pilot with {"signoff": {"by": "someone else", "at": "2026-01-01", "name": "X"}, "amendments": []} or {"criteria": "abc", "baseline_days": -5}.
expected: A strict request model (HANDOFF section 4: request models forbid unknown fields) accepting only baseline_start/baseline_days/criteria with types and ranges; `signoff` and `amendments` are server-owned and never writable; a started pilot's amendment trail cannot be erased (R8 2.13: 'pre-register the pilot so the saving cannot be argued about afterwards').
actual: `data = {**cur['pilot'], **{k: v for k, v in inp.items() if k in PILOT_DEFAULT}}` accepts `signoff` and `amendments` because both are keys of PILOT_DEFAULT (lines 131-133, 150), and stores any JSON for `criteria`/`baseline_days`/`baseline_start` without checking; the page then crashes on `p.pilot.criteria[c.key]` (criteria-tab.tsx 27) if criteria is not an object. The amendment appended at line 152 is itself replaced by the client's `amendments` in the same merge order (client value wins, then line 152 appends to the client's list).
evidence: routes_savings.py 131-133, 145-156; no pydantic model; frontend criteria-tab.tsx 26-27 assumes an object.

verdict.corrected_title: PUT /sites/:id/pilot has no request model: it stores any JSON for the pilot fields and lets the client write the signoff record (and, before start, forge amendments); a null criteria crashes the pilot page
verdict.reason: REPRODUCED live (owner) on the not-started Lahore site 37b2fd882dcb, then restored exactly (GET before == GET after): PUT {signoff:{by:'someone else',at:'2026-01-01',name:'X'}, amendments:[{...forged}], bogus_field:1} -> 200 with the signoff and forged amendments stored; PUT {baseline_days:-5, baseline_start:12345, criteria:'abc'} -> 200 stored as-is; PUT {criteria:null} -> 200 stored null. Code: routes_savings.py 131-133 PILOT_DEFAULT includes 'signoff' and 'amendments'; 150 merges any key in PILOT_DEFAULT with no type/range check; no pydantic model (contrary to HANDOFF section 4 'request models forbid unknown fields'); pilot_put writes no store.audit row (only lines 70, 125, 173 audit). criteria-tab.tsx 27 and review-tab.tsx 87 index p.pilot.criteria[c.key]: null throws (page crash); a string renders 'undefined' in every input (no crash). CORRECTION to the finding: after start the amendment trail cannot be erased - line 152 sets data['amendments'] from the STORED list plus the new entry, overriding the client's; the client's amendments win only before start (forgeable pre-registration history), and the signoff can be overwritten after start (an amendment line records only the key name). BY-DESIGN: nothing in DESIGN_LOG/HANDOFF 8-9; plan 9.3 UI-13 'Review and start locks the tabs; later edits are amendments' presumes a server-owned record. Permission start_pilot is admin-only (auth.py 40), so the actor is the customer's own admin or a buggy client, which caps this at medium: integrity of the pre-registration (R8 2.13) and a self-inflicted blocked pilot page.

verdict.corrected_title: Switchback tiles include the carry-over credit (zero on the demo today) without showing it, the 'unadjusted' subtitle misdescribes the figure, and the counterfactual-vs-switchback agreement check is absent

title: Monthly PDF prints 'Diesel saved 0 L' when the genset was unmetered, and prints a saving for days whose claim is withheld without any mark
label: bug
steps: At a site whose genset has no fuel signal for the whole month (every day `genset_unknown`, levers.genset null), generate the Monthly savings report; also include a day with `claim_withheld: import_unknown`.
expected: 'not metered' (as the web ledger says, savings-ledger.tsx 56) rather than a zero; a withheld day marked in the daily rows (plan 8.4 never over-claim; DESIGN_LOG round 3/4 withheld days claim nothing).
actual: verify.summary stores `litres_saved: round(litres, 1)` summing `or 0.0` (line 1055, 1079), never null, and reports.py line 117 prints it with ' L'; the daily rows (146-148) print `saving_native_rs` and `fidelity` only, so a withheld day shows a rupee figure with 'confirmed' beside it and no withheld mark; the CSV has no claim_withheld column either.

verdict.reason: REPRODUCED by code and partly live. verify.py:1055 `litres += d.get("litres_saved") or 0.0` and :1079 `"litres_saved": round(litres, 1)` never yield null even when every day's litres_saved is None (compute_day verify.py:748 `None if g_unknown`); reports.py:115-119 prints `num(nat.get("litres_saved", 0), unit=" L")`, which renders '0 L' (the generated Faisalabad PDF prints '0 L', the farm PDF even '-0 L' from a small negative), whereas the web ledger (savings-ledger.tsx:56) prints 'not metered' when all days are unmetered or litres_saved is null. Daily rows reports.py:146-148 print saving_native_rs and fidelity only, so a day with claim_withheld (verify.py:745-746) and fidelity 'confirmed' shows a rupee figure beside 'confirmed' with no mark; the CSV header written at reports.py:142-143 and confirmed in results/verify-pagesD/fsd-monthly.csv is day,...,saving_native_rs,saving_tuned_rs,fidelity,plan_ids with no claim_withheld column. No demo site currently has a genset_unknown or withheld day (GET /api/sites/{id}/savings for all four: genset_unknown_days 0, no claim_withheld), so the unmetered case is confirmed from the code path, the PDF/CSV layout live. BY-DESIGN: DESIGN_LOG rounds 1-2 ('Unmetered genset fuel is unknown, litres null, never zero') and rounds 3-4 (withheld days claim nothing) are the product's own rules, which the PDF breaks; HANDOFF 8.B covers only the web pages showing the withheld claim. Medium: a customer-facing money document contradicts the page and shows a saving on days the engine withheld.

title: Bills can only be entered and rebuilt for the site's first connection
label: feature-gap
steps: On a site with two grid connections (plan 9.6: the Karachi feed mill, 'two connections, the MDI line on two bills'), open Savings > Bill comparison > Enter a bill. Try to enter the second connection's bill.
expected: Plan 8.2 layer 3: 'the DISCO bill per connection and settlement period'; the dialog lets the person pick the connection and the list says which connection each bill belongs to.
actual: add_bill uses `conns[0]` for the rebuild and stores `conns[0]['id']` (lines 1248-1270); the dialog (bill-dialog.tsx) has no connection field and the BillCard (bills-panel.tsx 52-59) never shows `connection_id`. The second connection's bill is rebuilt against the first connection's tariff and meter series.
evidence: verify.py 1244-1275; bill-dialog.tsx 74-83; bills-panel.tsx 52-94.

verdict.reason: REPRODUCED by code: verify.py:1266 `rebuild_bill(site_id, conns[0], p0, p1, ...)` and :1270 stores `conns[0]["id"]`; the accepted fields at :1261 carry no connection; bill-dialog.tsx BillForm :26-36 and billBody :75-83 have no connection field; bills-panel.tsx BillCard :52-94 never reads connection_id although the Bill type has it (types/api.ts:859). The rebuild also reads telemetry.minute_grid per site (verify.py:1284), so there is no per-connection meter series either. Live: the scratch demo's Karachi feed mill has one connection (demo.py:71 seeds one; GET /api/sites/e9941b41c70b lists one), so the plan-9.6 'two connections, the MDI line on two bills' step cannot be walked on the demo, but the code path is unambiguous. BY-DESIGN: nothing in DESIGN_LOG ('Tariffs and bills' entries cover reading dates and ICP only) or HANDOFF 8-9 records a one-connection limit; plan 8.2 layer 3 asks for 'the DISCO bill per connection and settlement period'. Medium: at a two-connection site the second bill is rebuilt against the first connection's tariff and the whole site's import, so the 2 % check is meaningless there; not a claimed-saving figure, so not high.

title: Bill comparison stores the typed peak/off-peak units and MDI but never shows or diffs them against the rebuilt lines; only the total is checked and only the actual arm's bill is rebuilt
label: feature-gap
steps: Enter a bill with Peak units, Off-peak units and MDI filled in; open the bill card.
expected: R8 2.12 Bill comparison: 'the DISCO bill as entered or uploaded vs the rebuilt bill for both arms, line by line: units by window, MDI kW and charge, adders, net-billing credit, GST'; plan 6.3 step 13: every line's residual logged.
actual: BillCard reads only `real.total_rs`, `real.reference` and `real.previous_reading_date`; the typed units_peak, units_off_peak and mdi_kw (stored in `real`, verify.py 1262) are never shown or diffed against the rebuilt energy and demand lines; only the rebuilt (actual) arm's bill is produced (rebuild_bill, verify.py 1278), no native-arm bill.
evidence: bills-panel.tsx 52-94; bill-dialog.tsx 147-150; verify.py 1262, 1278-1288.

verdict.corrected_title: Bill comparison stores the typed peak/off-peak units and MDI but never shows or diffs them against the rebuilt lines; only the total is checked and only the actual arm's bill is rebuilt
verdict.reason: REPRODUCED by code and live: bills-panel.tsx:56-67 reads real.total_rs, real.reference and real.previous_reading_date only; the lines table :72-90 lists the rebuilt lines with no printed-value or residual column; verify.py:1262 stores units_peak, units_off_peak and mdi_kw in `real` and nothing reads them afterwards (grep over backend/gridlytics/*.py); difference_pct (:1267) is on the total; rebuild_bill :1278-1288 prices the measured import/export only, no native-arm bill for the billing period. Live GET /api/sites/37b2fd882dcb/bills: the mall's sample bill carries rebuilt.lines with units_kwh ('Energy peak', 'Energy off-peak') and rebuilt.mdi_kw, which could be diffed against the typed figures but are not. The dialog itself promises 'shows the difference line by line' (bill-dialog.tsx:118). BY-DESIGN: no DESIGN_LOG or HANDOFF 8-9 entry defers this; plan 9.3 UI-12 says 'Bill comparison (line by line, the 2 percent check)', plan 6.3 step 13 'every line's residual logged'. The 'both arms' bill is R8 2.12 wording and secondary; the plan's layer 3 is real vs rebuilt, which is only checked on the total. Medium: an operator types units and MDI that are silently discarded, and a total within 2 % can hide compensating line errors that 6.3 wants turned into overrides.

verdict.corrected_title: Switchback painting and pilot start ignore the control tier: a monitor-tier site can paint a calendar and start a pilot, after which the switchback result compares native settings with native settings; the Savings ledger never says the plan was only recommended
verdict.reason: REPRODUCED live as owner at 1440 on the monitor-tier Lahore mall (GET /api/sites/37b2fd882dcb: tier monitor, capture present): /sites/37b2fd882dcb/pilot?tab=calendar shows tab C unlocked with 'Paint the calendar' enabled (screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f64857cc-0ca7-5cbb-b665-d2b474fb2fb8/scratchpad/audit/results/verify-pagesD/shots/owner-1440-sites_37b2fd882dcb_pilot_tab_calendar.png); /savings?view=switchback shows 'No switchback calendar yet' with the 'Paint the calendar' CTA (switchback-panel.tsx:25-31); the ledger heading is 'Ledger by lever' (savings-ledger.tsx:58). Code: routes_savings.py:80-94 and verify.plan_switchback :1125-1143 check permission, dates and the lock only; pilot_start :159-174 checks capture and calendar only; compute_day :715-718 labels monitor days recommendation_only, but switchback_result :1190-1230 regresses actual cost on block arm regardless of fidelity, so at a monitor site (both arms run the native settings) it would print a 'Saving per day' that is noise. evidence: criteria-tab.tsx 12-19; routes_savings.py 131-133; grep of verify.py/reports.py shows no use of `criteria`.

verdict.reason: REPRODUCED by code and live: grep of backend/gridlytics/*.py for criteria, min_saving_pct, reserve_adequacy_pct, fidelity_pct, fee_multiple, forecast_pv_nrmse_max hits only routes_savings.py:131-133 (PILOT_DEFAULT); nothing in verify.py or reports.py evaluates them. Frontend hits are criteria-tab.tsx:12-19 (inputs) and review-tab.tsx:87 (lists the values); fee-card.tsx:17-19 checks a hard-coded 'one third' against fee.within_one_third, not the stored fee_multiple; savings-kpis.tsx has no reserve-adequacy, fidelity-share or criteria tile. Live GET /api/sites/{id}/pilot returns the six defaults for all four sites, none started, and no page or report compares them with a result. CRITERIA and PILOT_DEFAULT hold no genset run-hours gate and no cycling clause (plan 15.3: EFC per day at most 1.1x the tuned baseline's; R8 2.13 'without deeper cycling than baseline'). BY-DESIGN: BACKEND_ASKS.md:34 already lists the missing genset gate (that part is a known ask), and HANDOFF 8.C lists VER-07's go/no-go template as not built, but tracker EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md:174 marks VER-10 [x] including 'the pilot write-up template with the pre-registered gates of Part 15.3' while no read-out of the stored criteria exists anywhere: new evidence that the tracker is wrong, not a restated open item. Medium: pre-registration is the pilot's proof device (plan 8.5, 15.3; R8 2.13), and without scoring the 'gates nobody moved' are decorative and OnyxLeaf cannot show a go/no-go; no figure is wrong today.

title: Forecast panels show almost no actuals: the overlay starts at the latest issue's belief time, which is re-issued every 15 minutes
label: spec-mismatch
area: Forecasts page: PV/load fan charts and outage chart
steps: Open /sites/:id/forecasts on any active site (demo or real). The PV and load fans and the outage chart draw `actual` from GET /sites/:id/forecasts/{kind}. forecast.page() builds `actual` only from the issue's belief_time (t0) forward (lines 414-424: minute_grid(site_id, t0, t1)). plans.tick() re-issues the forecast on every 15-minute tick for every active site (plans.py 391-400; scheduler.py 19-35, 71), so the latest issue is always under 15 minutes old and `actual` holds 0 or 1 step. The page then prints 'No actuals yet for this issue: they appear as dots as the 15-minute steps pass' (forecast-panel.tsx 67) forever, since the next issue resets it.
expected: Plan 9.3 UI-08 / R8 2.8: each panel is a 48-hour fan chart 'with actuals drawn over the past 24 hours' so an operator can see how the forecast tracked. The fixture outages.json (forecast.actual length 0) shows the state the page lives in.
actual: The 'Actual' series is empty or one dot; the chart's x-axis starts at belief_time so there is no past to draw; the 'now' mark (fan-chart.tsx 61) sits at the left edge.
evidence: forecast.py page(): `t1 = max(t0, min(now // 60 * 60, t0 + STEPS * STEP_S))`, `g = telemetry.minute_grid(site['id'], t0, t1)`; plans.py tick(): `bundle = forecast.issue(site, t0, save=save, now=now)` with t0 = align(now); frontend FanBody passes `actual={padded(f.actual, t.length)}` and `nowTs={f.belief_time}` (forecast-panel.tsx 53-65, 82). API_CONTRACT.md UI-08 row documents 'now line at belief_time'.

verdict.reason: Reproduced live. Code: forecast.py:438-455 page() builds `actual` only from the issue's belief_time t0 up to now. plans.py tick() calls forecast.issue(site, align(now), save=True) on every tick, and scheduler.py:71 ticks at :00/:15/:30/:45 +20 s (GRIDLYTICS_SCHEDULER=1 is set on the running uvicorn, pid 191). I polled GET /api/sites/{id}/forecasts/{pv,load,outage} for all four demo sites (verify-pagesC/c01.py, waitc01.out). Just after the 07:15:20 UTC tick, all 12 answers had belief age 0.5 min and actual length 0. The array can only reach length 1 just before the next re-issue resets it. Screenshot verify-pagesC/shots-after-tick/owner-1440-sites_6d4db49bf87e_forecasts.png shows 'No actuals yet for this issue: they appear as dots as the 15-minute steps pass' under both the PV and load fans (forecast-panel.tsx:67). The x-axis starts at the 'now' line (nowTs=belief_time, forecast-panel.tsx:64), so there is no past to draw. Spec: UI-08 in EMS_BUILD_PLAN.md:724 ('fan charts and actuals') and line 1045 ('quantile bands against actuals'), and R8-ux-pages.md:330 ('actuals drawn over the past 24 hours'). Nothing in DESIGN_LOG or HANDOFF 8-9 settles this. API_CONTRACT only describes the now line, and that is not a decision to drop the past. Medium: a spec feature is effectively missing and the on-screen promise never comes true. The accuracy cards still show skill, so it is not high.

title: 'Schedule adherence 80 %' is shown when no schedule exists: the Beta(8,2) prior is presented as a measured share and the 'No announced schedule yet' branches are dead
label: ux
area: Outages page KPI row and model card; Forecasts outage panel
steps: Create a grid-connected site, enter no load-shedding schedule, let a tick issue the outage forecast. GET /sites/:id/outages -> kpis.adherence = 0.8 and forecast.issue.adherence = 0.8. The Outages KPI tile reads 'Schedule adherence 80 % - announced windows that came true', the model card reads '80 % - The share of past announced windows in which the grid actually went down', and the Forecasts outage panel reads 'Schedule adherence 80 %'.
expected: With no announced windows the pages should say so (the code even has the texts 'No announced schedule yet' / 'No announced windows yet'), and a prior should be badged as a prior (plan 5.3 cold start 'flagged "prior" on screen'; R8 2.7 model card).
actual: forecast._adherence() returns a_hit/a_n = 8/10 = 0.8 when `windows` is empty (lines 307-315), issue() stores it as a number (line 393), routes_telemetry.outages copies it to kpis.adherence (line 237). The frontend null checks never fire: outages-page.tsx 66, outage-model-card.tsx 187-188, forecast-panel.tsx 89.

title: Genset litres are hard-coded 'estimated' and never estimated: metered sites are labelled 'from the fuel curve', unmetered sites show 0 L and Rs 0 fuel cost
label: bug
area: Genset page KPIs, run log, fuel cost
steps: (a) Site with a flow meter (plan 9.6: the Faisalabad textile plant; any source sending genset_fuel_l): GET /sites/:id/genset -> kpis.estimated = true although litres are the metered column; the page shows the 'Estimated' badge, sub 'from the fuel curve', and the runs header 'Litres (estimated)'. (b) Site whose source sends genset_running/genset_power_w but no genset_fuel_l: `cur['litres'] += nan_to_num(NaN)` = 0 per row -> kpis.litres 0, fuel_cost_rs 0, every run 0 L, still badged 'Estimated from the fuel curve' although nothing was estimated. Compare the Savings page for the same site: verify.py 228-253 estimates curve litres where fuel is unmetered and names the source (litres_source meter/curve), so Savings says 'Metered' or an estimated figure while Genset says 0 L 'Estimated'.
expected: R8 2.11: litres 'measured or estimated with the method badge'; 'No fuel metering: litres carry the badge Estimated from fuel curve everywhere' (i.e. a curve estimate exists); per run the 'source of litres: meter, tank delta, fuel curve, manual'. The genset KPI and runs should use the meter where read and the curve (a, b, rated_kw, power) otherwise, and set `estimated` from what was done.
actual: routes_telemetry.py 302-313: `cur['litres'] += float(np.nan_to_num(d['genset_fuel_l'][i]))`, line 318-319: `"fuel_cost_rs": round(litres * price, 0), "estimated": True`. Frontend genset-page.tsx 41-43 and genset-runs.tsx 189 render whatever the flag says.
evidence: verify.py: `from_curve = on & np.isnan(fuel_meas)` ... `curve += ...(plant.gen_a * p_meas + plant.gen_b * plant.gen_kw) / 60`; `out['litres_source'] = 'curve' if from_curve_any else 'meter' if read else None`. twin.py 467 writes a fuel column for demo sites, so the demo hides case (b) and shows case (a).

verdict.reason: Code: routes_telemetry.py:302-319 sums only the metered column (`cur['litres'] += np.nan_to_num(genset_fuel_l)`) and hard-codes `"estimated": True`. telemetry.raw (telemetry.py:362-375) returns NULL fuel as NaN, so unmetered litres become 0 L and fuel_cost_rs becomes Rs 0. A synthetic run of the copied loop (verify-pagesC/c04_sim.py) gives 'unmetered fuel: 0.0 L' for a 2 h run. Case (a) is reproduced live: GET /api/sites/{id}/genset gives estimated=true on all four demo sites, while GET /savings for the same sites gives energy.litres_source='meter'. Screenshot verify-pagesC/shots/owner-1440-sites_6d4db49bf87e_genset.png shows Faisalabad '159 L Estimated - from the fuel curve' and the column 'Litres (estimated)'. Plan 9.6 (EMS_BUILD_PLAN.md:755) gives that plant a flow meter, and twin.py:467 writes the metered fuel column. This breaks a settled rule: DESIGN_LOG:224 'Unmetered genset fuel is unknown (genset_unknown, litres null), never zero', and the web BUILD_NOTES:36 'not metered, never 0'. It also breaks R8-ux-pages.md:384/390 (litres measured or estimated, with the method badge and the litres source). Severity raised to high: on every site without a fuel meter, which R8 treats as the common case, the owner sees 'Fuel cost, 14 days Rs 0' and 0 L after hours of genset running. That is a wrong money figure, not just a mislabel. Line drift: the frontend lines are genset-page.tsx:41-42 and genset-runs.tsx:21, not 189.

title: Genset runs and the outage log count rows, not minutes: a blank sample ends a run or outage, and 5/15-minute sources under-count genset kWh, load ratio, genset minutes and unserved kWh
label: bug
area: Genset run log and KPIs; Outages log and KPIs
steps: Genset: telemetry.raw() returns only stored rows (telemetry.py 362-375). For a 5-minute CSV or OEM source each row stands for 5 minutes, but genset_page adds `genset_power_w/60000` and `genset_fuel_l` once per row (lines 309-310): kWh and litres are 5x (15x) too low while `hours` comes from timestamps (line 315), so load_ratio = kwh/(hours*rated) is 5x too low and every run is flagged 'under the minimum load' (genset-runs.tsx 203, genset-page.tsx 35). A 1-minute source with one NaN genset_running row inside a run: `on = NaN == 1` is False (line 304), the run is closed and a new one 'starts' at the next row, inflating `starts` and the run count. Outages: telemetry.outages() (telemetry.py 475-498) does the same: `genset_minutes += 1` and `unserved_kwh += unserved_w/60000` per row, and a NaN grid_present row ends the outage (`not down and cur is not None`), splitting one outage into two events, while the forecaster's own run detection bridges 15-minute gaps and 2-sample flickers (forecast._outage_runs 165-176; DESIGN_LOG rounds 1-2 'Load censoring').
expected: R8 2.11 / U3 3.7: 'a missing signal is unknown, not off'; DESIGN_LOG round 3: stage rules count minutes of data, not rows, 'so a 5- or 15-minute source' is treated like a 1-minute one. Runs and outages should scale each sample by the source interval (forecast.sample_minutes exists) and bridge gaps as the forecaster does, so the log's event count matches the hazard's.
actual: Per-row accumulation and NaN-as-off in both loops; the outage log's hint ('a gap in the data is not an outage', outages-page.tsx 111) is half true: a gap does not create one but a blank reading ends one.
evidence: routes_telemetry.py: `on = d['genset_running'][i] == 1` ... `cur['kwh'] += float(np.nan_to_num(d['genset_power_w'][i])) / 60000`; telemetry.py: `down = d['grid_present'][i] == 0` ... `if not down and cur is not None: out.append(cur)`; forecast.py: `OUTAGE_GAP_MINUTES = 15`, `FLICKER_MINUTES = 2`, `iv = sample_minutes(known)`.

verdict.corrected_title: Genset runs and the outage log count rows, not minutes: a blank sample ends a run or outage, and 5/15-minute sources under-count genset kWh, load ratio, genset minutes and unserved kWh
verdict.reason: Code: routes_telemetry.py:302-315 adds genset_power_w/60000 once per stored row and treats `NaN == 1` as off. telemetry.py:480-492 (outages) adds genset_minutes += 1 and unserved_w/60000 per row, and closes an outage on a NaN grid_present row. By contrast, forecast._outage_runs (forecast.py:139-149) bridges unknown minutes up to OUTAGE_GAP_MINUTES=15 and grid-up flickers of FLICKER_MINUTES=2. I ran both loops copied verbatim on synthetic sources (verify-pagesC/c04_sim.py). A 2 h, 100 kW run on a 200 kW set gives kWh 200/40/13.3 and load_ratio 0.5/0.1/0.04 for 1/5/15-minute sources, so a coarse source would be flagged under the minimum load. One blank genset_running row splits one run into 2 runs. One blank grid_present row splits a 60 min outage into 30 + 29 min. A 5-min 60 min outage reports genset_minutes 12 (truth 60) and unserved 1.2 kWh (truth 6.0). Coarse sources are an accepted input: DESIGN_LOG:126 (stage rules count minutes of data, not rows, for 5/15-minute sources) and forecast.sample_minutes. The demo twin is 1-minute with no blanks, so this is not visible live. One part of the claim is overstated: litres are a per-sample sum (telemetry SERIES_KIND genset_fuel_l='sum'), so a coarse source reporting litres per interval is not under-counted. Hence the corrected title. Medium: wrong log figures and fuel-related KPIs at sites with coarse or gappy sources.

title: 'Preliminary' is dropped as soon as a forecast reaches stage 1 (3 days of data), against the rule 'Preliminary until 28 verified days and stage 1'
label: spec-mismatch
area: Forecasts page stage badges and issue line; Outages 'Stage 0 prior' badge
steps: Seed a site with 4 days of data. PV reaches stage 1 at days_ok >= 3 (forecast.py 86), load at have_days >= 3 (line 224). GET /sites/:id/forecasts/pv -> stage 1, preliminary false. actual: `"preliminary": f["stage"] == 0` on the server and `stage === 0 ? "Stage 0, Preliminary" : "Stage N"` on the client; a 4-day-old site shows unmarked stage-1 forecasts.
evidence: forecast.py page(): `"preliminary": f["stage"] == 0`; forecast-words.ts: `export const stageLabel = (stage) => ... stage === 0 ? "Stage 0, Preliminary" : `Stage ${stage}``; stage-card.tsx 50-53.

verdict.reason: Code: forecast.py:455 `"preliminary": f["stage"] == 0`. PV reaches stage 1 at days_ok >= 3 (line 88) and load at have_days >= 3 (line 208). forecast-words.ts:33-34 labels only stage 0 'Preliminary', and forecast-panel.tsx:34, stage-card.tsx:50-53 and plan-header.tsx follow the same stage-0 rule. Live: all three demo grid sites show 'Stage 1' with no Preliminary mark (API c01.py, preliminary false; screenshot shots-after-tick/owner-1440-sites_6d4db49bf87e_forecasts.png). title: A genset request can be answered again or a withdrawn one answered: answer_request does not check the request's status
label: bug
steps: POST /sites/:id/genset/requests/{nid} {outcome: done} on a request whose status is 'withdrawn' (moved earlier, or no plan in force) or already 'answered not_now'. The row becomes status 'answered', outcome 'done', scored_at now.
expected: Only a pending request can be answered, once; the outcome feeds the fidelity score (R8 2.11, DLV-07), so a withdrawn request (the run was asked for again at another start) must not be scorable and an answer must not be overwritten silently.
actual: `UPDATE notifications SET status = 'answered', outcome = ?, scored_at = ? WHERE id = ?` with no status predicate; the UI only offers buttons on pending rows (genset-advice.tsx 270-277) so the API alone exposes it.
evidence: alerts.py 283-287.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in code. alerts.py:280-292 answer_request selects the row by id and site, then runs 'UPDATE notifications SET status = 'answered', outcome = ?, scored_at = ? WHERE id = ?' with no check on status. It also moves the matching genset_request_{start} alert from 'resolved' to 'closed', overwriting its note (e.g. 'Moved earlier to HH:MM'). The route (routes_telemetry.py:343-352) adds no check. There are three consequences. (1) The UI can reach this too, not only the API: the genset page polls every 60 s (genset-page.tsx:59), so a request the tick withdrew can still show Done or Not now (genset-advice.tsx:46,59) and be answered. (2) A withdrawn request that is then answered has status 'answered', so genset_requests (alerts.py:239-246) counts it as 'asked' (status != 'withdrawn'). For an overlapping run that later moves earlier again, len(later) < len(asked) and the re-ask is skipped, which defeats the DESIGN_LOG rule that one run holds one pending request and an earlier start is asked again. (3) A second answer silently overwrites the first. The claim that the outcome 'feeds the fidelity score' is not true yet: a grep shows the outcome is only written and displayed, because DLV-07 scoring is [~]. Not reproducible live: no demo site has any request rows right now, and I did not create any. Low: a narrow window and a manual-start-only path.

title: Manual forecast refresh skips the same-quarter observed-outage protection and can store a blind outage issue over an observed one (refresh is also open to operators)
label: spec-mismatch
steps: (a) auth.need('run_jobs') with run_jobs = {admin, operator, analyst} (auth.py 41); stage-card.tsx 39 says 'for an administrator, an operator or an analyst'. (b) The route calls forecast.issue(s, now_ts()) with save=True: save_forecast does INSERT OR REPLACE on (site, kind, belief_time = align(now)) (telemetry.py 602-608), replacing the issue the current plan was built on at the same quarter, and without plans._keep_observed_outage (plans.py 385-400), the rule DESIGN_LOG rounds 1-2 settled ('a same-quarter re-solve never replaces an issue that observed an outage with a blind one').
expected: R8 2.8 / plan 9.4: retrain or refresh is for owner and analyst; the plan's 10.5 permission table has no run_jobs. A manual refresh should either go through the same protection as the tick or not overwrite the tick's stored issue.
actual: Operators can refresh; a refresh while a batch is more than OBSERVED_LAG_MIN minutes in flight can store a blind issue over an observed one, which the scores and the forecasts page then show.
evidence: routes_forecasts.py 29-31; telemetry.save_forecast; plans.tick 398-400.

verdict.corrected_title: Manual forecast refresh skips the same-quarter observed-outage protection and can store a blind outage issue over an observed one (refresh is also open to operators)
verdict.reason: Code checked. routes_forecasts.py:27-31 calls auth.need('run_jobs') and then forecast.issue(s, now_ts()) with save=True. auth.py:41 sets run_jobs = {admin, operator, analyst}, and the operator's Forecasts page shows the 'Refresh forecasts' button (screenshot operator-1440-sites_6d4db49bf87e_forecasts.png). forecast.issue (forecast.py:419-431) always saves the outage issue through telemetry.save_forecast, which is an INSERT OR REPLACE on (site, kind, belief_time) (telemetry.py:602-605). Only plans.tick wraps this in _keep_observed_outage (plans.py:359-401). forecast.outage marks 'observed' only when the last known grid minute lags by at most OBSERVED_LAG_MIN = 2 (forecast.py:37,392). So a refresh during an outage, with the edge's rows more than 2 min behind, replaces the quarter's observed issue with a blind one. Plans._saved_outage (plans.py:350-356) then reads that blind issue as the prior for any later same-quarter re-solve. This breaks the DESIGN_LOG:187 rule ('A same-quarter re-solve never replaces an issue that observed an outage with a blind one'). The rule exists, so the bug is not by design, and HANDOFF 8-9 does not list it. The operator-permission half is weak: plan 9.4 gives retraining to the analyst, but a refresh only re-issues what the tick does every 15 minutes. The trigger window is narrow (same quarter, lagging edge, manual click), and the refresh itself does not re-plan. Not reproduced live: it needs a staged outage with lagging telemetry, and the POST would write scratch state. Low.

verdict.reason: Code and API agree. forecast.scores (forecast.py:544-559) computes last7 as the mean of v[-7:], the last 7 scored rows rather than 7 calendar days. score_day (forecast.py:484-541) writes baseline_value only for load (same day last week) and outage (schedule-only), never for PV, and every row has horizon_class 'day_ahead'. GET /api/sites/{id}/forecasts/scores?days=30 as analyst on all four demo sites returns PV baselines 0/12, load 8/12, outage 12/12, and no skill metric. accuracy-cards.tsx:19 labels the tile '<metric>, last 7 days'. Plan 5.5 (line 477) wants PV 'skill scored per horizon class' against smart persistence. The plan's Forecasts-ready gate (line 106) is PV skill of 25% or better at the 6-24 h class. Yet the tracker marks FOR-04 ('the skill scoring per horizon class'), FOR-10 ('metrics of Part 5.5 by horizon class') and UI-08 ('accuracy to date by horizon class') as [x]. title: Switchback native blocks are never applied by the live tick: at a real site a 'native' block still runs the plan
label: feature-gap
steps: 1) `grep -rn arm_on backend/gridlytics` shows the switchback arm is read only by verify.py (compute_day 711-716, switchback_result 1205-1215) and demo.py:162 (`_policy_for`, the twin). plans.tick (plans.py:391-500), delivery.py, routes_plans.py and routes_edge.py contain no reference to the switchback table or arm. 2) Paint a calendar on a real closed-loop or advisory site, start the pilot, and let a native block begin: the 15-minute tick keeps solving and storing an active plan, the edge keeps receiving signed slot tables (advisory: the plan page keeps showing the table and 'Mark as applied'). 3) The nightly compute_day labels the day `native_block` and claims nothing; switchback_result then treats the day's measured cost as the native arm.
expected: Plan 8.2 and VER-08 ('the arm applied to the plan: a baseline block plans native'): during a native block the tick issues a release / plans native so the inverter runs its own settings, and the switchback compares measured plan days with measured native days.
actual: Only the demo twin follows the calendar. At a real site both arms of the switchback are plan days; the 'Saving per day, adjusted/unadjusted' KPIs on the Switchback tab and the carry-over credits are computed from mislabelled days, and the ledger forgoes the claim on those days. The pilot's primary field evidence (Part 15.3 gates, 8 weeks of switchback) cannot be produced.
evidence: plans.py has no `arm_on`/`switchback` call; demo.py:162-164 is the only place the arm changes a policy; verify.py:715-716 and 1205-1215 rely on the arm having been applied. Tracker EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md line 172 marks VER-08 `[~]`; HANDOFF §8 and DESIGN_LOG do not list this gap.

title: Closed-loop days are 'confirmed' by construction: days with control paused, released to native, a failed plan or an offline edge still claim their saving
label: bug
steps: 1) verify.compute_day 707-729: `elif site.get('demo_link') or tier == 'closed_loop': fidelity = 'confirmed'` with no look at plans.active_at / held plans (plans.py:452-455, 504-522 `control_paused`, `released_to_native`), edge acks, read-back mismatches or fallback events. 2) On a closed-loop site add a `pause_control` or `force_native` override for several days: the tick stores plans as `held` and the edge gets a signed release (plans.py:677-686), so the inverter runs native. 3) Run the nightly compute_day for those days.
expected: Plan 8.3/8.4: fidelity is a gate per day (confirmed / partial / not applied); a day on which no plan was in force, or the edge fell back to native, claims nothing (as advisory days without an applied row do, 722-723).
actual: Every closed-loop day is `confirmed`, `claimed_rs == saving_rs`, and it counts toward the 28 verified days and the fee check. The claimed figure on such days is replay error plus any manual genset action, not a product saving. The same holds for demo sites under a pause (test_fix_r2_savings.py:448 checks the twin runs native but not that the day claims nothing).
evidence: verify.py:717-729 branches; nothing in compute_day reads `plans` status; control_state in routes_sites.py:43-44 already knows 'edge_offline' for closed loop but savings ignores it.

title: Tuned baseline has no HOMER cycle-charging rule; at off-grid sites all 8 tuned variants simulate identically to native, so the 'beat the tuned baseline' gate is void
label: spec-mismatch
steps: 1) verify.TUNED_VARIANTS (541) and tuned_table (544-555): two or four rows (00:00 charge_grid|hold|self_use, 06:00 pre, peak-window discharge). fit_tuned (563-607) sets `window = (-1,-1)` for a site with no connection (572), so the table is two rows of self_use/hold. 2) twin.native_policy gives every table `genset: -1` (twin.py:192-193, the native operator rule), and twin.simulate's outage branch (twin.py:367-433) ignores `mode` entirely; an off-grid series has grid=0 every minute. 3) Hence at the demo farm `arms['tuned']` equals `arms['native']` minute for minute; on-grid genset sites' tuned arm runs the genset exactly as native.
expected: Plan 8.1: 'the best static table of the same brand grammar ... and at genset sites additionally HOMER-style cycle charging with a set-point SoC. Claims must beat the tuned baseline'; Part 15.3 gates and the fee check are against the tuned baseline; tracker VER-12 is marked `[x]`.
actual: The second comparator is a copy of the first wherever the genset lever dominates (off-grid, outage-heavy sites), so 'Saving against a tuned table' and the fee's `min(native, tuned)` provide no protection against claiming what a well-set cycle-charging rule (fewer starts, the set near rated output, charging to a set point) would also have saved.
evidence: verify.py:541-555, 572, 583; twin.py:192-193, 367-433; DESIGN_LOG 2026-11-06 'a grid search over eight static TOU tables' records the table search but not the missing cycle-charging comparator; EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md line 108 VER-12 `[x]`.

title: Monthly MDI lever is claimed, and its actual peak taken, on days whose claim was withheld for genset/battery data; an unseen genset's peak cut is credited to the plan
label: bug
steps: 1) verify.summary: `m[3] += int(d['fidelity'] in CLAIMING and not imp_unknown)` (1066) ignores `claim_withheld`, whereas `verified` (1059) and `m[5]` (1068) exclude withheld days. `m[0]/m[1]` (1062-1064) take the month's peaks from every non-import-unknown day, including `genset_unknown` days. 2) `mdi_claimed` (1075) adds the month's MDI lever to `claimed_rs` (1078) and to the fee basis (1076, 1113) whenever any day of the month is confirmed/partial. 3) Make a month where every day is withheld `genset_unknown` (a parallel set with blank columns, compute_day 746): each day row shows 'Claim withheld' and claimed_rs 0, yet the KPI 'Claimed on verified days', the fleet MTD and the fee check show the month's MDI rupees.
expected: A day withheld because its genset may have run unseen must not feed any claimed figure (compute_day's own comment at 743-746: its energy 'the grid levers or the carry-over would credit without its fuel'); the MDI lever should be claimed only from months with at least one claiming, non-withheld day, and the actual peak should not be taken from genset_unknown days.
actual: An unseen grid-parallel genset run lowers the actual arm's import peak; the month's MDI lever credits that cut to the plan and it is claimed and fee-counted although every day says the claim is withheld.
evidence: verify.py:1059-1076, 1078, 1113; compute_day 736-757 sets `claim_withheld` per day but the month aggregation only honours `import_unknown`.

title: One MDI rate (the last scored day's) prices every month's MDI lever; wrong across tariff versions and Tariff F seasons
label: bug
steps: 1) summary() loops over all days of the period and keeps a single `rate = d.get('mdi_rate') or rate` (1069), then prices every month with it: `mdi_by_month = {k: (...) * rate ...}` (1073). 2) Each day's `mdi_rate` already carries its month's factor: tariffs.vectors 754 `rate_rs_per_kw = fixed x fixed_factor x _seasonal_factor(month)`, and `_seasonal_factor` is the multiplier in season and 0.0 outside it (tariffs.py:490-495). 3) Request a period at a seasonal (season_months) connection spanning an off-season month followed by an in-season month, or a period across an approved tariff change.
expected: Each month's MDI lever priced at that month's own rate (the per-day row already stores it).
actual: The last day's rate is applied to all months: an off-season month gets charged the in-season rate (over-claim), or in the reverse order the in-season month's MDI lever is zeroed; a tariff change mid-period misprices the earlier month.
evidence: verify.py:1045, 1069, 1073; tariffs.py:490-495, 752-755; compute_day stores `mdi_rate` per day (754).

title: Headline 'Saving', the ledger by lever, the daily bars and both CSVs include withheld days' partial levers and non-claiming days; CSVs carry no claimed/withheld column
label: ux
steps: 1) compute_day 736-742: on an `import_unknown` day the grid levers are None but genset, wear and carry_over are still summed into `saving_rs`; on a `battery_flow_unknown` day the grid and genset levers are summed. summary 1050-1053, 1078 adds every day's levers and `saving_rs` regardless of fidelity (not_applied, native_block, recommendation_only) or `claim_withheld`. 2) Frontend: the first KPI tile shows `native.saving_rs` as 'Saving against the native settings' (savings-kpis.tsx:32-33, claimed only in the sub-line); the ledger table's levers and 'Saving, all days' (savings-ledger.tsx:69-80) and the bars (daily-savings-chart.tsx:14) use the same figures. 3) Exports: routes_savings.savings_csv header (routes_savings.py:66-69) and the report CSV (reports.py:142-155) have `saving_native_rs` and `fidelity` but no `claimed_rs` or `claim_withheld`, so a withheld day exports as fidelity 'confirmed' with a rupee saving; the PDF daily rows (reports.py:146-148) likewise.
expected: Plan 8.4 'never over-claim' and 8.5 (CSV 'so a dispute can be re-run'): the largest number on the page and every exported row should be the claim or be unmistakably labelled; a withheld day should contribute nothing (or null) to any headline and carry its withheld reason in exports.
actual: A reader of the page or the CSV takes the unclaimed, partially-levered total as the saving; a day whose claim is withheld for an unknown import still adds a carry-over credit (energy possibly charged from the unmetered grid) to the headline.
evidence: verify.py:742, 1050-1053, 1078; savings-kpis.tsx:32-33; savings-ledger.tsx:69-80; daily-savings-chart.tsx:14; routes_savings.py:66-69; reports.py:115-125, 142-155.

title: CSV annexes lack the tariff version and capture version the plan requires, while the PDF says the tariff versions are 'dated in the CSV annex'
label: spec-mismatch
steps: 1) reports.generate writes the PDF footer 'Native capture version N; tariff versions as dated in the CSV annex' (159-160). 2) The report CSV header (142-143) is day, import_kwh, export_kwh, pv_kwh, load_kwh, genset_hours, litres, outage_minutes, peak_kw [, saving_native_rs, saving_tuned_rs, fidelity, plan_ids]: no tariff version, no capture version. 3) routes_savings.savings_csv (66-69) has neither plan ids nor versions.
expected: Plan 8.5 and VER-03: 'the data behind every figure downloadable as CSV with the tariff version, the capture version and the plan ids'; the day row already stores `native_capture_version` and `icp_case`.
actual: The PDF promises a column that does not exist; a dispute cannot be re-run from the export alone.
evidence: reports.py:142-143, 159-160; routes_savings.py:66-69; tracker VER-03 `[~]`.

title: Off-grid per-day carry-over is noisy: the per-day ledger drifts from a continuous replay by thousands of rupees (known, open)
label: bug
steps: 1) compute_day prices the carry-over as `(e_end_actual - e_end_native) x v_end` (733) with `v_end = eta_d x c_next - wear` and, off-grid, `c_next` the genset's marginal cost at `night_load_ratio` (669-675, 610-627): Rs 172-184/kWh at the farm. 2) Both replays restart each day from the actual SoC, so the native arm is re-credited daily for energy the actual arm holds. 3) DESIGN_LOG round 5 'Open': paired 11-day farm rebuilds show the per-day ledger minus the continuous replay ranging -6.2k to +7.9k Rs, the carry-over lever 'swings by tens of thousands of rupees and largely offsets the genset lever'.
expected: HANDOFF 8.A.1 done-criterion: the per-day ledger tracks the continuous replay within about Rs 1k over 11 days on several seeds before any off-grid pilot; Part 8.2's carry-over is meant to be priced, not to dominate the ledger.
actual: Customers at an off-grid site see a per-day ledger whose sign on a given day is set by the carry-over valuation rather than by fuel burnt; monthly totals can be over- or under-stated by several thousand rupees per 11 days. Documented as open; not fixed.
evidence: verify.py:610-627, 669-675, 733; docs/DESIGN_LOG.md round 5 'Open: the per-day carry-over at off-grid sites is noisy'; HANDOFF.md §8.A.1.

title: Metering factor (VER-13) not fitted or applied: both arms and the bill rebuild use raw CT energy and MDI; no out-of-band factor is ever raised as a data finding
label: feature-gap
steps: 1) rebuild_bill calls `tariffs.rebuild(...)` without `energy_scalar`/`mdi_scalar` (verify.py:1278-1288; defaults 1.0 at tariffs.py:506-507). 2) price_arm (107-126) applies no factor to either arm. 3) The `bills` table stores real/rebuilt/difference_pct only (add_bill 1268-1270); nothing fits a factor from two bills or tests a third, and nothing flags a factor outside 0.97-1.03.
expected: Plan 6.3/8.2/8.4 and VER-13: one energy scalar and one MDI scalar per connection fitted on two bills, tested on a held-out third, applied to both arms before pricing; a factor outside 0.97-1.03 is a data finding; the 2% bill gate closes only when a held-out bill passes.
actual: A CT that under-reads against the DISCO register (a load the inverter does not see) scales every rupee lever and the MDI lever silently, and the bill comparison can never reach the gate. The bearable-basis half of VER-13 is in place (energy_factor, recovered_taxes_rs), the factor half is absent.
evidence: verify.py:1278-1288; tariffs.py:506-507, 536-544; EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md line 110 VER-13 `[ ]`; HANDOFF §8.C.

title: Days scored mid-month keep a projected ICP case and scaled month totals; nothing re-scores a month at its end, after late data, a new capture or an approved tariff/FCA version
label: feature-gap
steps: 1) `_minute_prices` (69-92) settles the ICP case from `month_totals(site_id, conn, day)` (38-57), which before the month ends scales the metered minutes to date up to the whole billing month. 2) scheduler.nightly_company (scheduler.py:38-53) scores only yesterday; no job re-runs compute_day for the month's earlier days when the month closes or when `native_for_day`, an adder (FCA) or a tariff version changes. 3) At an ICP site, days 1-20 score 'below' (TOU rates); the month ends 'above' (flat ICP rate on every kWh). Days 1-20 stay priced at TOU rates in the ledger, the report and the fee check unless an operator presses Recompute (routes_savings.py:46-56: synchronous, 62-day cap, 5 s MILP bound per day).
expected: Plan 8.2: the ICP lever 'comes from the full-month counterfactual only'; 8.4: every day re-scorable with the inputs of its day; the month's figures should settle automatically once the month (and its FCA) is known.
actual: The month's rupees depend on when each day was scored; a month that flips ICP case, or whose FCA is approved after the days were scored, shows stale per-day levers.
evidence: verify.py:38-57, 74-81; scheduler.py:38-53; routes_savings.py:46-56.

title: Carry-over credit only at plan-to-native boundaries; a native block that hands over a fuller battery is uncredited
label: spec-mismatch
steps: 1) `_carry_over_credits` (1159-1176) skips every pair unless `a.arm == 'plan' and b.arm == 'native'`. 2) At a backup-mode native (holds 90-100 % while the grid is up) a native block ends full; the next plan block's first day spends that energy with no debit. 3) switchback_result adds only plan-to-native credits to the plan's saving (1224-1227).
expected: Plan 8.2: 'at every block boundary the bill engine credits the arm that ends with more stored energy by (E_end_A - E_end_B) x v_end'. On a native block's last day the plan arm's end energy can be approximated from the native day's `baseline` replay versus the actual, or the native-to-plan hand-over priced at the measured E_end difference between the last native day and what the plan's first day inherits.
actual: Asymmetric accounting: with self-use natives it under-claims, with hold/backup natives it over-claims the plan block's first day. The docstring records the omission as a limit; DESIGN_LOG does not.

title: Switchback 'adjusted' saving is fitted with 5 coefficients on as few as 6 days and the 15 %/Rs 300 agreement check is absent
label: feature-gap
steps: 1) switchback_result returns a result once `len(y) >= 6` and both arms present (1216); the regression (1221) has an intercept, the arm, PV, load and outage hours: 5 parameters, so with 6-8 days the adjusted figure has one to three degrees of freedom and no uncertainty is reported. 2) No code compares the switchback saving with the counterfactual saving on the switchback levers (Part 8.2's 15 % or Rs 300/day rule; VER-08).
expected: A minimum sample well above the parameter count (or a confidence bound as Part 15.3's 'lower 80 percent confidence bound' needs) and the agreement statistic shown beside the two estimates.
actual: A noisy adjusted figure is shown as a KPI ('Saving per day, adjusted') from the sixth priced day; the counterfactual-versus-switchback disagreement that the plan calls 'a finding, not a rounding' is never computed.
evidence: verify.py:1216-1230; switchback-panel.tsx:39-46; tracker VER-08 `[~]`.

title: Report wording: the Preliminary sentence omits two of the four conditions, and the baseline at manual-genset sites includes an assumed operator rule the capture does not record
label: ux
steps: 1) reports.py:109 prints 'Preliminary. Fewer than 28 verified days, the month is not over, or a fuel adjustment of the period is not yet billed.' while verify.summary (1099) also requires a native capture and 8 switchback weeks; the web page lists all four (savings-page.tsx:48-53). 2) reports.py:159-160 states 'Figures are measured against a replay of the inverter's own settings on the same day's sun, load and outages', but at a manual-start genset site the native arm also applies twin.simulate's operator rule 'someone starts it when the lights would go out and stops it once the battery is charged' (twin.py:396-397), which is not part of any capture. 3) The 'Ledger by lever' table (121-125) sums all days including unclaimed and withheld ones without saying so.
expected: Plan 8.2: 'At genset sites the operator's genset actions are logged per arm and the genset stream is reported with its fidelity rather than claimed as blinded'; 8.5: the method stated; a lawyer-reviewed claim wording is owner task O9.
actual: A CFO reading the PDF is told the baseline is purely the inverter's settings and is given an incomplete reason for 'Preliminary'.

title: PV stage-1 fit slices history into 24 h blocks from the tick time, not local days: performance ratio and fan change with the time of day
label: bug
steps: Scratch company; write 15 local days of 5-minute pv_power_w for a 100 kWp/100 kW plant at 31.5N 74.3E equal to solar.pv_power(clear sky) x 1.0 on even local days and x 0.45 on odd days. Call forecast.pv(site, t0) with t0 = local midnight 2026-11-09, then 09:00, 12:00 and 15:00 the same day, and read pr and q05/q25/q50/q95 at tomorrow's noon step as a share of cs.
expected: The 14 whole days behind each tick are the same alternating clear/overcast history, so every tick should fit pr about 1.0 (the clearest days) and the same fan: q05 0.45, q50 0.725, q95 1.0 of clear sky. The plan (5.1) fits the ratio on clear-sky periods and the bands from day residuals, and the live tick runs this every 15 minutes.
evidence: forecast.py:75-87: h0 = t0 - 14*86400 on a 15-minute-aligned t0 and `sl = slice(d*1440, (d+1)*1440)`, so each 'day' runs from the tick's time of day to the same time next day and mixes the afternoon of one local day with the morning of the next. The per-slice ratios k_days average towards the mean, pr = quantile(k, 0.9) (line 92) drops, kn = k/pr (line 93) collapses to about 1 and so do the empirical quantiles kq (line 94). plans.build_problem reads q50 as PV and q25 as PVlo (plans.py:175-176) and optimise.py:306-317 sizes the outage reserve from Lc - PVlo, so an intraday plan can carry a PV q25 57 % above the midnight issue's and a collapsed uncertainty band; the Forecasts page's 'performance ratio' also swings through the day. Fix: slice on local-day boundaries (twin.day_start_utc / (ts+5h)//86400) and drop the partial first/last day.

title: Schedule adherence is updated per 24 h block from the tick time (windows split and pooled), so the posterior depends on when the tick ran and converges per day, not per slot
label: bug
steps: 28 days of 1-minute grid_present with a daily 14:00-16:00 window actually kept on 7 of the 28 days (hit rate 0.25). Call forecast._adherence(windows, grid, _window_mask(windows, ts)) once with the 28-day history starting at local midnight and once with it starting at 15:00 (what outage() builds at a 15:00 tick, h0 = t0 - 28 d).
expected: The same posterior either way: Beta(8,2) prior plus 7 hits in 28 windows = 0.395; per the plan (5.3, R5 4.3, tracker FOR-08 'adherence updates per observed slot') the update is per scheduled slot or window with separate start/end rates, converging in about 20 slots.
actual: 0.395 for the midnight-aligned history, 0.553 for the 15:00-aligned one (0.12 s snippet). A tick inside or after the window inflates adherence by pooling half of today's window with half of tomorrow's; the demo's Faisalabad site has exactly a 14:00-16:00 window.
evidence: forecast.py:310 `day_idx = (np.arange(len(grid)) // 1440)` partitions from h0, line 314 tests `mean(down[sel]) >= 0.5` over all in-window minutes of that block, so two half-windows from different calendar days are one trial and a hit on either counts. The value feeds p_down_s (line 368), the hard g = 0 rule once it passes 0.9 (line 383), the plan header (plans.py:413) and the Outages page KPI (routes_telemetry.py:235). Fix: iterate over window occurrences (local day x window) and count each as one Bernoulli trial.

title: Stage-1 PV with 3-6 days of data: the clearness quantiles are the stage-0 prior because the scaling term divides the median by itself
label: bug
steps: Evaluate line 94 with kn = [0.5, 0.6, 0.55, 0.7] and month_k = 0.88 (any site with 3 to 6 fitted days).
expected: The observed clearness level of the fitted days informs the quantiles (or the code states that the prior is used on purpose below 7 days).
actual: `np.median(kn) / max(1e-6, np.median(kn))` is 1.0, so kq == np.clip(K_PRIOR * month_k / 0.86, 0, 1.1) exactly (checked: [0.307 0.46 0.716 0.88 0.972 1.023 1.044]); the site's data only enters through pr.
evidence: forecast.py:94. The expression is a no-op by construction; the intent was presumably to scale the prior by median(kn) over the prior's own median (month_k). Impact is small because pr absorbs the level, but it is dead code masquerading as a fit and the first week of every new site runs on it.

title: PV fit and PV scoring read curtailed inverter output (pv_power_w) and ignore curtail_w, so zero-export sites fit a low performance ratio and are scored against their own curtailment
label: bug
steps: Demo Faisalabad (regime none, no export cap) or any real zero-export C&I site: once the battery is full late morning, surplus PV is curtailed. twin.simulate writes pv_power_w = available - curtail (twin.py:446, 465) and curtail_w separately (twin.py:468); a real inverter likewise reports produced, i.e. curtailed, PV. After 14 such days call forecast.pv at midnight and, next day, score_day.
expected: The capacity fit (plan 5.1: measured on physical power on clear-sky periods) and the daytime nRMSE use available PV = pv + curtail, which telemetry.minute_grid already exposes as g['curtail'] (telemetry.py:396). The clear-sky ceiling and the forecast describe what the plant can deliver; curtailment is the optimiser's own decision (K[t]).
actual: pvm = g['pv'] (line 81) and k_days (line 87) are computed on curtailed output; the clearest days are also the most curtailed, so pr = quantile(k, 0.9) is biased low and every quantile is capped at pr x cs (line 103-104). score_day uses col = g['pv'] (line 503), so curtailed midday hours count as forecast error and feed the forecast_bust alert and the accuracy tiles. The Forecasts page then shows a 'performance ratio' below 1 on a healthy plant.
evidence: forecast.py:80-87, 103-104, 503; twin.py:446, 465-468; telemetry.py:393-396 (curtail column available). Magnitude not measured here; it scales with the share of days the battery fills before noon.

title: Critical load comes only from the onboarding form, defaults to 0 kW for every hour, and a zero makes the outage reserve rule inert with no warning
label: feature-gap
steps: Onboard a site in the web app leaving 'Critical load' at its default (site-form.ts:74 `critical_load_kw: Array(24).fill(0)`, accepted by the zod rule `v >= 0` at site-form.ts:152), activate it, let a tick run, read the plan steps' critical_kw and the reserve.
expected: Plan Part 4.1 (line 301) and 5.2: Lc[t] is the 75th percentile of observed load during adequately backed outages per hour of day (or from a backup-load point), with the template as fallback and a data-quality warning; the plan's headline value is holding reserve for the next forecast outage.
actual: forecast.load reads twin.critical_share(site) = data.critical_load_kw only (lines 207, 211, 245) and caps it at q75; no learned profile exists (the plan's critical_load_profiles table with source 'learned' is absent). With the default zeros Lc = 0, deficit = max(0, Lc - PVlo) = 0 in optimise.py:310-312, so R[t] is only the sigma widening and no reserve is ever held; activation (routes_sites) and the onboarding review (tab-review.tsx:72 prints '0 kW at most') do not flag it.
evidence: forecast.py:206-211, 245; twin.py:83-85; sites.py:60 default [0.0]*24; optimise.py:306-317; frontend site-form.ts:74,152. The tracker defers the learned estimate to FOR-07 (stage 2), but Part 5.2 places it with censoring, stage-independent, and a silent zero default is a product defect on its own.

title: Load accuracy is scored against shed (censored) minutes and the persistence baseline over a different slot set, so the page shows inflated load nRMSE and a non-comparable baseline
label: bug
steps: A site with a daily 2-hour grid loss during which only the backed-up circuits run (load falls 60 %). forecast.load censors those minutes (lines 201, 152-193) and, correctly, forecasts the full demand. Next day forecast.score_day(site, day) is run by alerts.nightly.
expected: Plan 5.2: censored samples leave the training set and the baselines; the nRMSE should skip censored slots (or score served load against a served-load forecast), and the baseline RMSE should be computed over the same slots as the forecast's so the 'baseline' column on the Forecasts page is like for like.
actual: act = nanmean(g['load']) over all 96 slots (lines 503-504) includes the shed slots, so every outage day charges the forecast with the shed demand; the baseline (lines 517-521) is averaged over okp = ok & ~isnan(pers) while the forecast uses ok, so with gaps last week the two RMSEs cover different slots. The summary tiles (lines 553-556) and ScoresTable then mislead the pilot's 'beats persistence' gate.
evidence: forecast.py:496-522 versus censored_minutes (152-193) and the plan's censoring rule; the same censored_minutes mask is available in score_day via minute_grid.

title: No PV skill or smart-persistence baseline and only one horizon class are scored, although tracker FOR-04 and FOR-10 are marked done
label: spec-mismatch
steps: Open the Forecasts page after a week of scores, or query GET /api/sites/{id}/forecasts/scores: the pv rows carry value only (baseline null) and every row has horizon_class 'day_ahead'.
expected: Plan 5.5 / R5 6: PV skill = 1 - RMSE_model/RMSE_smart_persistence per horizon class (0-2 h, 2-6 h, 6-24 h, 24-48 h), where smart persistence is the clear-sky profile times yesterday's same-hour index (6-24 h) or the last hour's index (0-2 h); the WP5 gate is skill >= 25 % at 6-24 h. FOR-04 ('skill scoring per horizon class') and FOR-10 ('metrics of Part 5.5 by horizon class') are [x] in EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md lines 125 and 131.
actual: score_day writes a single 'day_ahead' row per kind (lines 515, 531); the PV row has no baseline_value, so the accuracy tiles show an nRMSE with nothing to judge it against and the product cannot report the gate it pre-registered. title: Bill rebuild prices the whole reading interval with the versions in force on the reading date; the optimiser and ledger price each day with that day's version

Plan 6.1 leaves the February proration open and gates the 2% rebuild on re-running at the first 2027 bill. A reading interval that spans a schedule's effective date should be priced per day by the version in force (DISCOs bill such intervals pro rata by days), or by one documented rule shared by the bill engine, the vectors and the ledger.

evidence: tariffs.py:517-523 (`on = period_end`; card_for, calendar_for, _tax_factor_energy all at `on`), 555 icp_rule(on), 608/611 prosumer(on); vectors at 687-690 use `on = t0` local date. Probe in the scratchpad: bill marginal 26.45 against vector 31.10 for 25 Jan 2026 03:00.

title: Rebuilt bill floors at zero and discards the excess export credit (no carry-forward); bearable_rs goes negative
label: bug
steps: 1. Take an A-2(c) connection on net_metering_legacy. 2. Rebuild October 2026 with 20 kW import all day and 300 kW export from 09:00 to 15:00, so the off-peak period ends in surplus. 3. Result: total_rs 0.0, credits_rs 1,525,510, gross bill before credit about 326,753, recovered_taxes_rs 79,157.51, bearable_rs -79,157.51. 4. Nothing records the unused credit, so the next month's rebuild starts with no brought-forward balance. The same applies to net_billing when exports x NAEPP exceed the gross bill.
expected: Plan 6.3 step 9 and R9 13 step 9 say the bill never goes negative, but the excess credit rolls to the next cycle, or is paid quarterly under Prosumer reg. 14(2). Legacy sites need carry-forward balances (R9 17.7; tracker TAR-02, marked [x], lists "settlement and carry-forward"). The bearable cost of a zero bill cannot be below zero unless a carried credit is accounted for.
actual: `total = max(0.0, bill_amount + s235 + flat - credit)` silently drops the credit beyond the bill. bearable_rs = total - recovered then subtracts GST and s.235 that the floor already absorbed, giving a negative bearable cost. There is no carry-forward state anywhere. The vectors still value every surplus kWh at the surplus or NAEPP rate, so in surplus months the optimiser and ledger disagree with the rebuilt bill. Both the surplus month and the following month differ from the DISCO's bill.
evidence: tariffs.py:604-611 (credit), 637-639 (floor, recovered, bearable). grep finds no carry/brought-forward state in backend/gridlytics. Probe output: `3 legacy total 0.0 bearable -79157.51 recovered 79157.51 credit 1525510.0`.

title: FCA recognised only by the exact key "fca": a second FCA on the same bill drops out of the ICP price, and its negative-FCA exemption is lost
label: bug
steps: 1. Take an ICP-eligible B-2(b) connection whose November 2026 off-peak total is above its baseline. 2. With the shipped adders, the vectors' above-case c_imp is 23.325 and the rebuild's 1-kWh marginal is 23.32 (they agree). 3. Approve an adder with key "fca_sep", +2.5624, billing_months ["2026-11"]. adders_for's docstring says two months' FCAs billed together are two keys, and R9 6.2 says NEPRA bundles FCAs or moves one to the next bill. Now the vector stays at 23.325 while the bill charges 25.93 per ICP kWh. 4. Approve "fca_aug_neg" at -1.5 with negative_exempt_icp True. The bill now charges it on the ICP units (24.41) although the rule exempts them; the vector is still 23.325. 5. verify.summary's fca_billed (verify.py:1097) treats a month whose FCA has another key as not yet billed.
expected: Positive FCAs apply to ICP incremental units and negative FCAs do not (R9 5, SRO 2409), whatever key a bundled or late FCA is stored under. The optimiser's ICP price must equal the bill's (plan Part 4 rule, OPT-06).
actual: vectors' add_icp sums only `a["key"] == "fca" and rate > 0` (line 697). rebuild exempts a negative FCA from ICP units only when `a["key"] == "fca"` (line 596). verify checks `a["key"] == "fca"`. A second FCA key therefore makes the optimiser under-price ICP units by that FCA x 1.015, and a negative second FCA is wrongly charged on ICP units.
evidence: tariffs.py:596, 697; verify.py:1097. Probe output: `A no 2nd FCA: vec 23.325 above bill 23.32`, `B +fca_sep 2.5624: vec 23.325 bill 25.93`, `C +neg fca under own key: vec 23.325 bill 24.41`.

steps: Rebuild a D-2(b) month: the DSS line bills 3.23 Rs/kWh on every unit (adder 'dss', billing_months all, exempt only icp_units and lifeline). Adders have no per-category rate.
expected: R9 7: Rs 3.23/kWh, but 43 paisa for protected residential up to 200 units and for agricultural tube wells (2023 structure, [S], to confirm on a bill). Adders need a per-category rate or a category exemption list.
actual: D-2 tube-well sites are overcharged about Rs 2.80/kWh (about 10% of the D-2 rate) in the bill, the vectors and the ledger. Adder exemptions such as lifeline, prepaid and evcs are never matched against the connection either.
evidence: tariff_data.py:98-100; tariffs.py:592-600 (only icp_units and the negative-FCA case are honoured); R9 section 7 table, DSS row.

title: A TOU calendar version that leaves a month out, or lists one twice, is accepted; the missing months then have no peak at all
label: bug
steps: 1. POST /api/tariffs/versions with kind tou, key xwdisco and body {"seasons":[{"months":[12,1,2],"peak":["17:00","21:00"]}]}, then approve it. 2. For March to November, peak_window returns (-1,-1) (line 334), so is_peak_local is always False. Every B-2 minute is then priced and billed off-peak (22.83), and the optimiser stops discharging into the evening peak. A month listed in two seasons silently takes the first. A window with start == end gives no peak.
