3. Count the stops before the first control inside <main>: logo, 3 fleet links, site switcher, 9 to 11 site links, Add a site, 4 company links, company select, account, Sign out, alerts bell, account menu.
expected: A visually-hidden-until-focused 'Skip to main content' link as the first focusable element, targeting <main id="main" tabIndex={-1}>.
actual: <main id="main"> exists (app-shell.tsx:111), but nothing links to it. The <aside> sidebar is first in the DOM (lines 94-96), so a keyboard user must tab through the whole menu on every page. Landmarks help screen-reader users only, not sighted keyboard users.
evidence: grep -i 'skip to|#main' over src returns nothing. The DOM order is aside (Sidebar, sidebar.tsx:38-75) -> TopBar -> main.

title: Muted text fails 4.5:1 on the page background, on table headers and on selected cards
label: bug
expected: At least 4.5:1 for these 12 to 14 px texts.
actual:
4.44:1 on bg, 4.28:1 on surface-2 and 4.22:1 on brand-soft: all fail AA.

title: Recharts 3 makes each chart a focusable role=application inside a role=img wrapper: unnamed tab stops, one per Fleet row
label: bug
steps:
1. Open /fleet with sites that have a 7-day saving.
2. Tab through the Sites table: after each row's links and stamps comes an extra stop on the sparkline's <svg>.
3. Do the same on Battery (Daily cycles), Genset (Fuel curve) and Savings (daily chart).
expected: Charts wrapped as a static role=img are not focusable; pass accessibilityLayer={false} (or tabIndex={-1}) to BarChart/LineChart. Otherwise expose the recharts keyboard layer with a proper name and without the role=img wrapper.
actual:
Recharts 3.10.1 defaults accessibilityLayer to true (node_modules/recharts/es6/chart/CartesianChart.js:24). RootSurface then sets tabIndex=0 and role="application" on the <svg> (es6/container/RootSurface.js:40-51). The app wraps each chart in <span|div role="img" aria-label>:
- spark-bars.tsx:10
- battery-charts.tsx:49
- genset-cards.tsx:23
- daily-savings-chart.tsx:16
That is a focusable control nested inside an element whose children are presentational (axe 'nested-interactive'). The svg gets no accessible name and captures arrow keys. On Fleet this adds one such stop per site row.
evidence: grep -rn accessibilityLayer src returns nothing (no override). RootSurface.js: `tabIndex = hasAccessibilityLayer ? 0 : undefined; ... role = hasAccessibilityLayer ? 'application' : undefined`.

title: Selects that write or reload on every change: arrow keys on Windows switch company, change member roles and suspend memberships

The select is then disabled while pending (busy(m), line 72), so focus drops and the intended role cannot be reached.

- company-switch.tsx:23 `onChange={(e) => ... setCurrentCompanyId(e.target.value)}`

Otherwise record in DESIGN_LOG why an activation is different from a switchback block start. Chaining through days withheld for data reasons (battery or genset blank) is fine.

steps: 1) Pick last month's period (up to 62 days) on the Savings page and press Recompute. 2) compute_range scores up to 62 days, each with the 5 s perfect-foresight solve (with_bound defaults to True), then `_recompute_forward` re-scores up to 62 more contiguous later days, keeping their bound. The first recompute of an old day after the merge always walks the full 62, because every later legacy row mismatches. 3) All of it runs inside the HTTP request. The answer is {"days": n} for d0..d1 only, so the toast 'Recomputed N days' (savings-actions.tsx:31) undercounts.
expected: Run the forward walk as a background job (the app already has a jobs module) or cap the request's total work. Return and show the number of later days re-scored.
actual: Up to about 124 day replays plus bound solves in one request, and an undercounted toast.
evidence: routes_savings.py:46-56 (the 62-day check covers d0..d1 only); verify.py:1165-1176; verify.py:739-758 (FORWARD_MAX_DAYS=62); verify.py:755 keeps with_bound where the row had perfect_foresight_rs; verify.py:947-983 `_bound` solves with time_limit=5.0.

title: 'Done when' evidence for 8.A.1 is not reproducible, and its Rs 1 match holds by construction on gap-free data
label: spec-mismatch
steps: 1) The DESIGN_LOG round 6 evidence table (lines 53-66: three farm seeds, Karachi, Faisalabad) comes from 'fresh paired 14-day rebuilds' scored by HEAD's ledger and by the change's. The harness is not in the diff (only verify.py, reports.py, two test files and docs changed). 2) With no restart in a period, the chained carry telescopes to v_N*G_N exactly, so 'Change minus cont. = 0' is an identity of the accounting. It shows the chain is wired correctly, not that per-day figures stopped swinging. Per-day spread is not reported: the carry-over and genset levers can still offset day to day, now at realised cost. 3) The rebuilds are gap-free twin telemetry. Each withheld dropout day restarts the chain and leaves one v_end-valued end term per segment (the original noise source), and no run measures the ledger against continuous replay with realistic dropout rates. 4) The committed tests cover 3-day chains only.
expected: Commit the paired-rebuild harness as an opt-in script or slow test, so the owner can reproduce the table. Report the per-day carry-over spread (for example max |carry_over| per day) before and after. Add one rebuild with injected dropouts (say 2 withheld days in 11) to show the ledger stays within about Rs 1k.
actual: The 'done when' is asserted in prose and cannot be re-run from the repository.
evidence: git diff --name-status origin/v1-build...origin/fix/offgrid-carry-over (no harness); DESIGN_LOG.md:53-69; verify.py:905 (carry = end - start, so the sum telescopes); test_fix_r6_savings.py DAYS = 3 days (line 20).

title: compute_day docstring says 'a claim never rests on what a dropout hid', but a claiming day with blank PV or load hands its distorted native state to the next days
label: spec-mismatch
steps: 1) Off-grid farm. On a claiming day, blank pv_power_w from 10:00 to 13:00 while battery and genset columns stay read. No withhold reason applies: imp_unknown is grid-only, wear_unknown needs the battery flow unknown, gen_unseen needs the genset columns blank. The day claims. 2) telemetry.filled counts the blank PV as 0, so native's replay sees no sun, drains, and may start its set. Its end state is too empty. 3) `_expected_start` restarts only when `not _claims(prev)` (verify.py:690), so the next claiming day starts native from that distorted state. Its claim moves by (realised cost - v_end) x deficit, the same mechanism the verifier measured at +1.1k to +2.9k for withheld days (DESIGN_LOG round 6). Under HEAD the next day restarted from the measured state.
expected: Either restart after any day with unread replay inputs, claiming or not, and accept the end-term noise; or withhold a day whose PV or load is blank for more than a threshold. At minimum, correct the docstring (verify.py:763-765) and add the case to DESIGN_LOG's known limits.
actual: The guard covers only non-claiming days, and the docstring states a guarantee the code does not give.
evidence: verify.py:671-677, 680-692, 761-768 (docstring); telemetry.py:417-421 (blank energy as zero); verify.py:913-915 (withhold reasons).

title: The Switch off dialog does not say that the company's sites stop being planned, its edge keys are refused and telemetry is lost
label: ux
steps: 1. On /admin/companies press Switch off for a company. 2. Read the dialog. 3. Compare it with what the server does to a switched-off company.
expected: For an EMS, the dialog says that while the company is off the scheduler stops solving its sites, its edge or partner API keys are refused (no new plans, telemetry posts refused), devices fall back to inverter-native mode when the current plan expires, and daily backups stop. actual: The dialog (lifted from Solarlytics, which has no devices) says only: 'Its 4 members are refused at the next request ... Its sites, plans and settings stay, and switching it on again lets them back in.' The guard refuses a disabled company's API key with 403 company_disabled (api.py:256). The plan's fallback is inverter_native on expiry (delivery.py:199). daily_all also uses company_files, so no daily copy is made while the company is off. Switching off the Karachi feed mill (closed_loop) would end its control with no warning.

title: A founder session cannot be ended: Sign out never reaches the server, and the token stays valid for all 8 hours
label: feature-gap
steps: 1. Sign in to /admin (password and code). 2. Press Sign out. 3. Call GET /api/founder/session with the same x-founder-session token.
expected: For a console that can switch off every company, reset any password and grant ownership, Sign out ends the session on the server. There should also be a way to end all founder sessions, at least when the founder password changes.
actual: Pressing Sign out makes no API call (it only clears sessionStorage), and the same token still answers 200 {"authenticated":true}. Tokens are stateless HMACs good for a fixed 8 hours with no idle timeout. Changing GRIDLYTICS_FOUNDER_PASSWORD_HASH does not invalidate them; only rotating GRIDLYTICS_FOUNDER_SESSION_SECRET and restarting does. No sign-out is recorded in the founder audit. This is inherited from Boxlytics' founder-auth.ts (the founder.py docstring says 'signing out is forgetting the token').
evidence: signout.cjs output: apiCallsOnSignOut=[]; sameTokenAfterSignOut=200 {authenticated:true}. backend/gridlytics/founder.py:17 and :56 (SESSION_SECONDS 8h); frontend/src/features/ops/founder-admin.store.ts logout() clears local state only.

In /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f64857cc-0ca7-5cbb-b665-d2b474fb2fb8/scratchpad/audit/bx-parity/: ix/styles.json has fonts []; public.json has fontsLoaded [] for every path. frontend/index.html:1-12 has no font link. frontend/src/styles/index.css:8. frontend/src/components/charts/use-echarts.ts:33.

area: Devices and control (UI-15) / Mode A table
steps: As analyst, open Karachi feed mill > Devices and control > 'The table to key in', Mon 9 Nov. Read slot 1. Compare with GET /api/sites/e9941b41c70b/control (compiled vs vendor_view).
expected: For a Sungrow forced-charge window the grammar field is target_soc, so the column should carry the charge target the intent states.
actual: Slot 1 reads 'Charge from grid, SoC % 44' with the intent 'Charge from the grid to 79 %'. After the re-solve at 12:15 the API shows soc_pct 62 (the floor, 61.7) against soc_target_pct 82.5 and the intent 'Charge from the grid to 82 %'. An installer keying this table would set a target 20-35 points below the plan's.
evidence: Screenshot: d1440/analyst-1440-sites_e9941b41c70b_control.png. API: grammar.fields ['start','end','target_soc']; vendor_view row {slot 1, mode charge_grid, soc_pct 62}; compiled slot {soc_floor_pct 61.7, soc_target_pct 82.5}. Code: delivery.py:227 (non-Deye, non-Huawei branch) uses `round(s['soc_floor_pct'])` for every slot. The Deye branch (line 221-222) uses the target for charge slots.

title: Demo sites always show 'Following plan (table applied)' or 'Following plan', contradicting their own applied log, alert and offline state
label: bug
area: Site header control chip (all site pages), Fleet
steps: As analyst, open Faisalabad > Devices and control, then Plan > Versions, then /alerts. Open Karachi feed mill > Overview while its data is stale.
expected: Advisory tier with no applied record today: 'Table not confirmed today'. Closed loop with data older than 5 minutes: 'Edge offline' (spec 9.2).
actual: Faisalabad's header says 'Following plan (table applied)'. The same page says 'APPLIED LOG: No table has been marked applied yet', the plan versions read 'Applied: No', and the open alert reads 'Today's slot table is not marked as applied'. Karachi (closed loop) says 'Following plan' next to 'Last data: 4 h ago' and 'No live data: the site is offline'.
evidence: Screenshots: d1440/analyst-1440-sites_6d4db49bf87e_control.png, crops/sites_6d4db49bf87e_plan-1.png, d1440/analyst-1440-sites_e9941b41c70b.png. API control {key: following, label: 'Following plan (table applied)'}, applied []. Code: routes_sites.py:43 `and not site.get('demo_link')` skips Edge offline; routes_sites.py:49-51 `'following' if ok or site.get('demo_link')`. The demo is meant to show the 'apply not confirmed' story (plan 9.6), and this override hides it.

title: Battery uncertainty never re-anchors at soc_max 95 %, so σ climbs to its 15 % cap and the reserve keeps the mill's battery full through every peak
label: bug
steps:
1) GET /api/sites/6d4db49bf87e/battery: sigma_pct 13.0, max SoC in the cycles list 95.0.
2) GET /api/sites/6d4db49bf87e/plan: plan fa7d5026e97a; read the hold_for_outage detail at 18:45 and breakdown.discharge_kwh.

expected: A full-charge anchor is reachable whenever the plan fills the pack to soc_max, or (spec 4.6) the optimiser is asked for an anchor slot when σ > 15 points. σ stays at a few points, and the reserve only covers the critical energy plus a modest margin.
actual:
Anchors need est ≥ 0.98, but every demo pack is capped at soc_max 0.95, so full-charge anchors never happen. σ grows 0.19 points an hour until an outage drains the pack to the low knee.
Implied σ in the reserve (R − Lc·h/η):
- Faisalabad: 0.125–0.15 on 29 Oct–1 Nov
- Lahore: 0.13–0.15 on all 11 days
The 2σ·E widening (up to 30 % of the pack) makes R ≥ the usable band. The current Faisalabad plan therefore holds 95 % for 48 h: Hold 95 % slots all day, discharge 2.17 kWh, 2,090 kWh imported in the peak. Its reserve detail is 184.8 kWh = 128.9 + 55.9 (2 × 0.13 × 215), which is more than the 182.75 kWh usable.
Faisalabad telemetry shows zero peak-window discharge on every plan day (28–31 Oct, 8–9 Nov).
The sigma_high alert says 'the plan will ask for a full charge to re-anchor', but the optimiser and plans code has no anchor logic. Rahim Yar Khan sits at σ 25, and its usable_kwh reads 0.0 at 53.5 % SoC.
evidence:
Code:
- battery.py:31: anchors = est >= 0.98 | <= soc_min + 0.02
- battery.py:55: the alert text
- plans.py:256: sigma0 = min(0.15, σ)
- optimise.py:312: R += 2·sig·En
- grep 'anchor' in optimise.py and plans.py: nothing
Current plan: fa7d5026e97a.
